definition.description: Lint files using ESLint. You must provide a list of absolute file paths to the files you want to lint. The absolute file paths should be in the correct format for your operating system (e.g., forward slashes on Unix-like systems, backslashes on Windows).

definition.name: agent_list
definition.description: List AI agent resources (appType: 'agent') in the project with their stack, runtime, durability and port. Read-only. Use `resource_list` for every resource type, and `agent_sessions` to inspect one agent's sessions. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

definition.name: agent_sessions
definition.description: List the sessions of a running AI agent resource (id, last activity, status, checkpoint size), or read one session's checkpoint when sessionId is set. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

sessionId.description: Session ID to read; omit it to list all sessions

definition.name: config_explain
definition.description: Explain one project file: whether Flisk generated it or the user owns it, its source, whether it is edited now, whether editing it blocks `up`, and what to edit instead. Run it before editing a file you did not write. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

file.description: The file, relative to projectPath (or to the server's directory) or absolute; it must be inside the project

definition.name: config_regenerate
definition.description: Regenerate the master config files in .flisk/.flisk-out/ from .flisk/project.json. A dry run by default, which returns the planned changes as data.changes (each file's status and lineDiff) with data.hasChanges; set dryRun to false to write them and get the same list, which discards hand edits in those generated files. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

dryRun.description: Default true: show what would change. false rewrites the files and discards hand edits in them

definition.name: config_verify
definition.description: Check that the generated files match .flisk/project.json and that every service.json is valid. Returns data.valid, data.errors, data.warnings and data.diffs; a drifted generated file is fixed with config_regenerate. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

definition.name: doctor
definition.description: Check whether this machine can run the Flisk stack (Docker, Tilt, ports). Read-only. Optionally set projectPath to include checks for a specific Flisk project. Returns data.ready and data.host.canUp; run it before `up`. For the state of a running stack use `status`; for whether generated files are consistent use `config_verify`.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

noPing.description: Skip pinging running services' health endpoints

definition.name: down
definition.description: Stop the running stack, optionally selecting its project with projectPath. It stops the running services and does not edit the project's files. Use `status` first to see whether a stack is running, set dryRun to preview, and start it again with `up`.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

dryRun.description: Show what would be stopped without stopping

definition.name: logs
definition.description: A bounded snapshot of recent logs from the running stack (default the last 200 lines, at most 10000), returned as text. Read-only. Optionally select the project with projectPath. Not a stream: call it again for newer lines. Use `status` first to find which service is failing, then pass services to narrow the output.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

since.description: Only logs newer than this, for example 30s, 5m, 1h

definition.name: network_list
definition.description: The Traefik URL of every frontend and API service, with its base path, port and whether it answers (running, stopped). Read-only. Use it to find where to open a service; use `status` for full readiness. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

definition.name: project_eject
definition.description: Write EJECTED.md with `flisk eject --json`: it lists the generated Tilt files and how to run the stack with plain Tilt, and copies, moves or deletes nothing. It changes the project, so it is refused unless confirm is true; dryRun returns the plan (data.generatedFiles, data.created) without confirm. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

confirm.description: Must be true to write EJECTED.md; without it only a dry run is allowed

dryRun.description: List the generated files and what would be written, without writing

definition.name: project_import
definition.description: Import the services in a directory's root docker-compose.yml as bring-your-own service.json files with `flisk import --json`, which runs the pinned flisk-import from npm (the first run needs network access). It writes without asking: set dryRun to get the plan only, and force to overwrite an existing service.json (force needs confirm: true unless dryRun is set). Returns data.written and the importer's output. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

dir.description: Directory with the docker-compose.yml, relative to projectPath or absolute (default: projectPath)

dryRun.description: Print the plan and write nothing

force.description: Overwrite an existing service.json

confirm.description: Must be true together with force (unless dryRun) to overwrite files

definition.name: project_info
definition.description: Project root, whether the generated master files exist (data.configured, data.missingFiles), and resource and stack counts. Read-only; a quick first call to learn whether a folder is a configured Flisk project. Use `config_verify` to check that the generated files match, and `status` for the running stack. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

definition.name: project_init
definition.description: Create a Flisk project with `flisk project --yes`: in projectPath (an existing directory; default the server's directory) write .flisk/project.json and generate its files, or, with template, clone a starter project into a new directory there (then call project_init again with projectPath set to the clone to configure it). Inside an existing project it refreshes that project's generated files instead and never overwrites its project.json. Returns the command's text output.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to an existing directory to create the project in (or to clone the template from)

template.description: Clone this starter project instead of creating a blank one

path.description: Template only: directory to clone into, relative to projectPath or absolute (default: the starter name, or its repository name)

agentSkills.description: Blank project only: write the Flisk agent skills and AGENTS.md (default true)

definition.name: project_templates
definition.description: List the starter templates project_init can clone (data.templates): each one's key, repo, description and, for a template pinned to a commit, the ref it checks out. Read-only; the same rows as `flisk project --list --json`. Pass a key as project_init's template.

definition.name: resource_create
definition.description: Scaffold a new service (service.json, Dockerfile, source and a test) with `flisk resource <name> --yes`, or register an existing directory that already has a service.json. Returns the command's text output. Without stack it uses the only existing stack or `main`, and fails when several stacks exist. Do not call it again for a resource that already exists: that rewrites its service.json and can assign it a new port (check with resource_list first). Call `up` afterwards to start it. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

name.description: Resource name (kebab-case)

type.description: Resource type (default backend). Redis, Qdrant, MinIO, MLflow, MySQL, MongoDB, ClickHouse, NATS, RabbitMQ, Mailpit and stripe-mock are frameworks: type database, queue, storage, mail or payment plus framework

stack.description: Stack to assign the resource to

framework.description: Frontend: react (default), vue, svelte, preact, lit, solid, qwik, vanilla, tanstack-router, next. Backend: hono (default), express, elysia, fastify, nestjs, koa, h3. Database: postgres (default, the shared Flisk Postgres), redis, qdrant, mlflow, mysql, mongodb, clickhouse (each its own container; the services that list it in dependsOn get its connection settings). Queue: nats (default), rabbitmq. Storage: minio (default). Mail: mailpit (default, local SMTP and inbox). Payment: stripe-mock (default, Stripe API emulator)

language.description: Backend language: bun (default), python, go, rust, node

port.description: Port within the type's range (default: the next free one)

features.description: Resource features to enable, for example prisma or drizzle

durability.description: Where agent sessions are checkpointed (type agent only): files or postgres

local.description: Frontend or backend only: scaffold it to run on this computer with no Docker or Tilt (a plain Vite config, a command in service.json), the way flisk create does by default

definition.name: resource_list
definition.description: List the selected project's services (resources) with their stack, type and port, whether or not they are running. Read-only. Use `status` for live state, `stack_list` to group them by stack and `agent_list` for agents only. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

definition.name: resource_restart
definition.description: Restart one running resource in the stack along with any active container resources that transitively declare `sidecarOf` on it (Flisk-generated Compose containers restart without rebuilding their image; local-process or non-container resources and projects using an imported Tiltfile fall back to `tilt trigger`); unrelated resources are not touched. It needs a running stack: start one with `up`. Set rebuild to true for a full Tilt update (rebuild the image and recreate the container, which re-reads the project .env). Names come from `resource_list`. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

resource.description: Name of the resource to restart

rebuild.description: Rebuild the image and recreate the container through Tilt

definition.name: resource_run
definition.description: Run a one-off command (a seed script, a migration, a status check) with the environment one resource has in the stack, and return its exit code, stdout and stderr (the last 64 KB of each; values from the project's .env files are masked). It runs any command, so it is refused unless confirm is true: ask the user first. A container resource must be running (start it with `up`); a local-process resource runs from its folder. No input is passed. Names come from `resource_list`. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

resource.description: Name of the resource whose environment the command gets

command.description: The program and its arguments, for example ["node", "scripts/seed.js"]

confirm.description: Must be true to run the command: it runs arbitrary code in the resource's environment

definition.name: runtime_check
definition.description: Read-only. Check that the installed Flisk CLI has its bundled runtime assets (engine, templates). Returns ok, assetRoot and what is missing; a source checkout reports ok: false because the assets exist only in a packaged install. projectPath is optional: a project-local install under its node_modules is checked too.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

definition.name: stack_assign
definition.description: Assign resources that have no stack yet to a stack (writes `stack` into their service.json). A resource already in a stack is refused unless move is true, which moves it out of its current stack. Returns the structured envelope: data.stack and data.assigned (name and service.json path of each resource), or errors with a code and suggestions (for example the valid resource names). Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

resources.description: Names of the resources to assign

move.description: Move resources that are already in another stack instead of refusing them

definition.name: stack_list
definition.description: List the project's stacks with their resource counts. Read-only. Use `resource_list` for the resources themselves. Set services to include each stack's service names, and verbose for its description. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

services.description: Include the service names in each stack

definition.name: status
definition.description: Show the live state of the stack: its stacks, resources, their ingress URLs and container ports, the stack-level ports, and Tilt readiness (data.tilt.readiness: ready, pending, failures, enabled; null when no Tilt answers). Read-only. Poll it after `up`. For the services a project defines whether or not they run use `resource_list`; for URLs only use `network_list`; for host checks use `doctor`. Optionally select the project with projectPath.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

definition.name: tool_add
definition.description: Add a tool by its everyday name (react, nextjs, fastapi, nodejs, postgresql, mysql, mongodb, rag, embeddings, llm-api) with `flisk tool add <tool> --json`, which runs the matching `flisk resource` command. data.status says what happened: resource (created; data.resource is the resource_create result), built-in (docker: nothing to do), manual (angular, tailwind, spring-boot, github-actions, jutro, policycenter: data.steps are steps to show the user; nothing was changed), or an error for a rejected tool (aws, google-cloud, azure, kubernetes): Flisk runs everything locally and never creates cloud resources, so do not work around it. Call `up` afterwards to start a new resource. Set projectPath when the MCP server is not running from the project root.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

tool.description: The tool to add, by id or everyday name ("Next.js", "google cloud"): react, nextjs, angular, tailwind, nodejs, fastapi, spring-boot, postgresql, mysql, mongodb, rag, embeddings, llm-api, docker, github-actions, weather, chart, services, jutro, policycenter, aws, google-cloud, azure, kubernetes

name.description: Resource name (default per tool, for example web, server, db); a name already in use is refused

stack.description: Stack to assign the resource to

dryRun.description: Preview the resource without writing files or reserving a port

definition.name: up
definition.description: Start the stack (or part of it) detached from the optional projectPath and return without waiting for it to be ready. Poll `status` for data.tilt.readiness.ready. Fails fast on an unknown service, an unsupported host, or a Tilt already running.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

only.description: Start only these services plus what they depend on and shared infrastructure

force.description: Replace a Tilt that is already running

dryRun.description: Show what would be started without starting

waitSeconds.description: How long to watch for an early failure before returning (default 15, max 60)

definition.name: foldkit_count_messages_by_tag
definition.description: Count retained Message history entries by tag, without payloads. Returns `{ counts: [{ tag, count }], totalCount, scannedFromIndex, scannedToIndex }` sorted by count descending. A cheap reconnaissance call before paging through history: it surfaces the high-frequency Messages worth filtering out, and with `changed_paths_match` it answers which Message tags touch a Model subtree. Accepts the same `since_index`/`changed_paths_match` filters as foldkit_list_messages.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.
Absolute history index to start from. Use the maybeNextIndex returned by a prior call to paginate.

Dot-string path patterns matched against each entry's changedPaths, in the same 'root'-anchored alphabet foldkit_get_model uses. An entry matches when any pattern matches any changed path. Patterns compare segment-by-segment for the length of the shorter side, so 'root.grid' matches every change inside the grid subtree, and 'root.grid.5.3' also matches a wholesale replacement recorded at 'root.grid'. '*' matches exactly one segment: 'root.cards.*.title'. Entries that did not change the Model never match. An empty list applies no filter. Patterns not starting with 'root' or '*' are rejected.

definition.name: foldkit_diff_models
definition.description: Diff the Models at two history indices server-side. Returns path-level changes `{ path, before, after }` sorted by path (numeric segments in numeric order), with values summarized. Each side is `{ _tag: 'Present', value }`, or `{ _tag: 'Absent' }` when the path does not exist on that side (a key or element that was added or removed). `from_index`/`to_index` follow foldkit_get_model_at semantics: the Model right after that entry was applied, with -1 for the initial Model. Pass `changed_paths_match` to narrow the diff to a Model subtree. Far cheaper than fetching two snapshots and diffing client-side; follow up with foldkit_get_model_at plus `path`/`expand: true` to read a changed subtree at full fidelity.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

from_index.description: Absolute history index of the diff baseline: the Model state right after this entry was applied. Use -1 for the initial Model.

to_index.description: Absolute history index of the diff target: the Model state right after this entry was applied. -1 addresses the initial Model.

anyOf.description: Dot-string path patterns narrowing the reported changes, in the same 'root'-anchored alphabet as changedPaths. A changed path is kept when any pattern matches it: patterns compare segment-by-segment for the length of the shorter side ('root.grid' keeps everything under the grid subtree) and '*' matches exactly one segment. An empty list applies no filter. Patterns not starting with 'root' or '*' are rejected.

definition.name: foldkit_dispatch_message
definition.description: Dispatch a Message into a Foldkit runtime, as if the application itself produced it. Requires the runtime to have configured DevToolsConfig.Message; without it, dispatch is rejected. Call `foldkit_get_message_schema` with no arguments to enumerate the variants, then with `variant_tag` to learn one variant's exact payload shape, before constructing the Message object. The runtime decodes the payload and returns a clean error if it doesn't match. To dispatch several Messages in order with one call, use foldkit_dispatch_messages.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

message.description: A Foldkit Message object to dispatch into the runtime. Must match the runtime's Message Schema. Call `foldkit_get_message_schema` with no arguments to see the available variant tags, then `foldkit_get_message_schema { variant_tag: "X" }` to learn one variant's exact payload shape. At minimum it has a `_tag` field naming the variant. The runtime decodes the payload and returns a clean error if it doesn't match.

definition.name: foldkit_dispatch_messages
definition.description: Dispatch an ordered batch of Messages into a Foldkit runtime in one call, first to last, as if the application produced them in quick succession. Prefer this over repeated foldkit_dispatch_message calls when staging state that takes several Messages: reproducing a bug, filling a form, or building a history fixture. Takes 1 to 100 Messages. Validation is all-or-nothing: the runtime decodes every payload against the Message Schema before dispatching any of them, and one invalid entry rejects the whole batch with an error naming its zero-based position, so there is never a partially applied prefix to clean up. On success the response carries acceptedAtIndices, the predicted history index for each Message in request order; the runtime may still record its own Messages between entries (for example a Command completing mid-burst), exactly as with rapid user input, and Messages excluded from history via excludeFromHistory are dispatched but never recorded, so entries after one land below their predicted index. Requires DevToolsConfig.Message, like foldkit_dispatch_message.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

messages.description: An ordered list of Foldkit Message objects to dispatch into the runtime, first to last. Must hold between 1 and 100 Messages. Each must match the runtime's Message Schema; call foldkit_get_message_schema to learn the shapes. The runtime decodes every entry before dispatching any of them, so one invalid entry rejects the whole batch with its zero-based position and nothing is dispatched.

definition.name: foldkit_get_init
definition.description: Read the runtime's initial Model, the Commands returned from the application's `init` function, and the Mounts that fired during the first render. The init entry is the synthetic row at index -1 in the DevTools panel; this tool exposes the same data without time-travelling the runtime. `maybeModel` is `None` until the runtime has finished its first render and recorded init, then stays `Some` for the rest of the runtime's life. `commands` lists init-time Commands in the order they were produced, each with its name, `args` (`Some(record)` when the Command declared an args schema, `None` otherwise), and `maybeSubmodelPath` (`None` before the result resolves, `Some([])` for a resolved top-level Command, or `Some(tags)` for a resolved Submodel Command); `mountStarts` lists Mounts whose elements appeared in the initial render, each with its name and `args` (`Some(record)` when the Mount declared an args schema, `None` otherwise).

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

definition.name: foldkit_get_message
definition.description: Read a single Message history entry by absolute index. The response carries the SerializedEntry (tag, message body, commands, mountStarts, mountEnds, timestamp, `isModelChanged`, `changedPaths` for leaf-level mutations, `affectedPaths` adding their ancestor paths). Each entry in `commands` carries the Command name, `args` (`Some(record)` when the Command declared an args schema, `None` otherwise), and `maybeSubmodelPath` (`None` before the result resolves, `Some([])` for a resolved top-level Command, or `Some(tags)` for a resolved Submodel Command). `mountStarts` lists Mounts that fired during the render after this Message; `mountEnds` lists Mounts whose elements were unmounted during that render. Each Mount carries its `name` and `args` (`Some(record)` when the Mount declared an args schema, `None` otherwise). For Submodel-routed entries (tag matches `Got*Message`), the entry also carries `submodelPath` listing wrapper tags from outer to inner and `maybeLeafTag` naming the innermost child Message. Model snapshots are not included; call foldkit_get_model_at with `index - 1` (before) and `index` (after) to inspect Model state around the entry.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

index.description: Absolute history index of the entry to read.

definition.name: foldkit_get_message_schema
definition.description: Describe the Message Schema for a Foldkit runtime so agents can construct valid payloads for `foldkit_dispatch_message`. Call with no arguments to receive a small variant index (every top-level variant's `_tag`, its payload field names, and which payload fields are themselves tagged-union shapes). Then call with `variant_tag: "ChosenVariant"` to drill in. The argument is a dot-separated path of variant `_tag` values: each segment names a variant, and the walker steps through the variant's single tagged-union payload field to reach the next. So `"GotMobileMenuDialogMessage"` narrows one level; `"GotMobileMenuDialogMessage.GotAnimationMessage"` narrows two levels of a Submodel chain. Discriminated unions deeper than the supplied path collapse to `{ "_summary": "union", "variants": [...] }` placeholders so the response stays compact even for deeply-nested apps; extend the path to drill further. `Schema.Option` fields render as `anyOf: [{_tag: "Some", value}, {_tag: "None"}]`. The full document follows the JSON Schema draft-2020-12 shape from `Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument`: `{ dialect, schema, definitions }`. Returns `maybeResult: None` when the runtime hasn't configured `DevToolsConfig.Message` (dispatch is also unavailable). Fields with no JSON representation, notably `Schema.instanceOf(File)` for user-uploaded files, render as `{type: "null"}`; those variants can't be dispatched via MCP because their values live in browser memory.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

Optional dot-separated path of variant `_tag` values. When omitted, the tool returns a small variant index (tag names plus payload field names plus a tagged-union indicator) so agents can enumerate the top-level union cheaply. When provided, the tool walks the path through each variant's single tagged-union payload field, narrows the schema along the chain, and collapses any union deeper than the path to a `{ "_summary": "union", "variants": [...] }` placeholder. Extend the path to drill further. Examples: `"ScrolledSidebar"` (one top-level variant), `"GotMobileMenuDialogMessage.GotAnimationMessage"` (two levels of a Submodel chain).

definition.name: foldkit_get_model
definition.description: Snapshot the current Model from a connected Foldkit runtime. By default the response is summarized (large arrays/records/strings collapse to `_summary` placeholders) to keep payloads small for AI agents. Pass `path` (e.g. 'root.session.user') to narrow to a subtree, and `expand: true` to receive the literal value at that path. Returns `{ value, atPath, summarized }`.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

Dot-string path into the Model anchored at 'root'. Examples: 'root', 'root.route', 'root.session.user', 'root.cards.0'. Matches the alphabet used by SerializedEntry.changedPaths so paths copied from one tool's output can be passed straight into the next. Defaults to 'root' (the whole Model).

When false (the default), large arrays/records/strings collapse to '_summary' placeholders to keep payloads small. Set true to receive the literal value at the path. Pair with `path` to drill in: a narrow path with `expand: true` is the cheapest way to read a specific subtree at full fidelity.

definition.name: foldkit_get_model_at
definition.description: Snapshot a historical Model after a given history entry was applied. Pass `index: N - 1` to read the Model just before message N. Same `path`/`expand` semantics as foldkit_get_model. Indices outside the retained history range (older entries are evicted past the rolling buffer) are rejected with the readable range. For the initial Model (and the names of Commands returned from the application's `init`), use foldkit_get_init.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

index.description: Absolute history index. Returns the Model state right after the entry at this index was applied. To inspect the Model immediately before message N, pass index N - 1. For the initial Model, use foldkit_get_init.

anyOf.description: Dot-string path into the Model anchored at 'root'. Examples: 'root', 'root.route', 'root.session.user', 'root.cards.0'. Matches the alphabet used by SerializedEntry.changedPaths so paths copied from one tool's output can be passed straight into the next. Defaults to 'root' (the whole Model).

When false (the default), large arrays/records/strings collapse to '_summary' placeholders to keep payloads small. Set true to receive the literal value at the path. Pair with `path` to drill in: a narrow path with `expand: true` is the cheapest way to read a specific subtree at full fidelity.

definition.name: foldkit_get_runtime_state
definition.description: Snapshot the runtime's DevTools state: history bounds, current paused/live status, and whether init is recorded. Returns `currentIndex` (the absolute index of the most recent Message, or -1 when none), `startIndex` (the earliest absolute index still retained in the rolling buffer), `totalEntries` (count of retained entries), `isPaused`, `maybePausedAtIndex` (`Some(index)` when paused, `None` otherwise), and `hasInitModel`. Use it to reason about what `foldkit_list_messages` and `foldkit_get_message` will see, and to detect whether the runtime is currently paused at a replayed snapshot.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

definition.name: foldkit_list_keyframes
definition.description: List the available keyframes (replayable Model snapshots) from a Foldkit runtime.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

definition.name: foldkit_list_messages
definition.description: List Message history entries from a Foldkit runtime. Filter server-side with `changed_paths_match` to ask in Model terms (which Messages touched this subtree), read the most recent entries with `from_end: true`, and paginate forward via `since_index` using the returned `maybeNextIndex` (the absolute index of the next matching entry). On busy histories (drag, scroll, keystroke flows), call foldkit_count_messages_by_tag first to learn what is worth filtering.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.
Maximum number of entries to return. Defaults to 50; max 500.
Absolute history index to start from. Use the maybeNextIndex returned by a prior call to paginate.

Dot-string path patterns matched against each entry's changedPaths, in the same 'root'-anchored alphabet foldkit_get_model uses. An entry matches when any pattern matches any changed path. Patterns compare segment-by-segment for the length of the shorter side, so 'root.grid' matches every change inside the grid subtree, and 'root.grid.5.3' also matches a wholesale replacement recorded at 'root.grid'. '*' matches exactly one segment: 'root.cards.*.title'. Entries that did not change the Model never match. An empty list applies no filter. Patterns not starting with 'root' or '*' are rejected.

When true, return the final `limit` matching entries (the most recent) instead of the first, still in chronological order. The natural first call when live-debugging: 'what just happened'. Cannot be combined with since_index.

definition.name: foldkit_list_runtimes
definition.description: List Foldkit runtimes (browser tabs) connected to every Foldkit dev server under the project root, or else to every dev server at the nearest root that encloses the project root, oldest dev server first. Each runtime carries `projectRoot`, the root of the dev server it belongs to, unless the MCP server uses a fixed relay address.

definition.name: foldkit_replay_to_keyframe
definition.description: Time-travel a Foldkit runtime back to a previous Model snapshot. Pass `keyframe_index: -1` for the initial Model, or a non-negative index for the state right after that history entry. The runtime is paused at the snapshot until foldkit_resume is called.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

keyframe_index.description: Index to replay to. Use -1 to jump to the initial Model (before any messages). Use a non-negative index to jump to the Model state right after that history index. Call foldkit_list_keyframes for the canonical replay points.

definition.name: foldkit_resume
definition.description: Resume normal execution of a Foldkit runtime that was paused by foldkit_replay_to_keyframe.

anyOf.description: Optional connection id of a specific Foldkit runtime. Defaults to the most recently connected runtime of the most recently started dev server. Call `foldkit_list_runtimes` to find runtimes in other applications, each with its `projectRoot`.

definition.name: list_log_entries
definition.description:
Use this as the primary tool to search and retrieve log entries from Google Cloud Logging.
    It's essential for debugging application behavior, finding specific error messages, or auditing events.
    The 'filter' is powerful and can be used to select logs by severity, resource type, text content, and more.

resourceNames.description:
Required. Names of one or more parent resources from which to retrieve log entries.
          Resources may either be resource containers (e.g. 'projects/[PROJECT_ID]') or specific LogViews (e.g. 'projects/[PROJECT_ID]/locations/[LOCATION_ID]/buckets/[BUCKET_ID]/views/[VIEW_ID]').
          For the case of resource containers, all logs ingested into that container will be returned regardless of which LogBuckets they are actually stored in - i.e. these queries may fan out to multiple regions.
          Projects listed in the project_ids field are added to this list.
          A maximum of 100 resources may be specified in a single request.

filter.description:
Optional. A filter that chooses which log entries to return.
          For more information, see Logging query language (https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/logging-query-language).
          Only log entries that match the filter are returned.
          An empty filter matches all log entries in the resources listed in resource_names.
          Referencing a parent resource that is not listed in resource_names will cause the filter to return no results.
          To make queries faster, you can make the filter more selective by using restrictions on indexed fields (https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/logging-query-language#indexed-fields) as well as limit the time range of the query by adding range restrictions on the timestamp field.
          Examples:
          - To find all error-level logs: 'severity="ERROR"'
          - To find logs from a specific GCE instance: 'resource.type="gce_instance" AND resource.labels.instance_id="1234567890123456789"'
          - To find logs containing a specific text message: 'textPayload:"database connection failed"'
          - To find logs within a specific time range: 'timestamp >= "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z" AND timestamp < "2025-01-01T01:00:00Z"'

orderBy.description:
Optional. How the results should be sorted.
          The timestamp asc option returns entries in order of increasing values of LogEntry.timestamp (oldest first), and the second option returns entries in order of decreasing timestamps (newest first).
          Entries with equal timestamps are returned in order of their insert_id values.
          We recommend setting the order_by field to "timestamp desc" when listing recently ingested log entries.
          If not set, the default value of "timestamp asc" may take a long time to fetch matching logs that are only recently ingested.

pageSize.description:
Optional. The maximum number of results to return from this request.
          Default is 50. If the value is negative, the request is rejected.
          The presence of next_page_token in the response indicates that more results might be available.

pageToken.description:
Optional. If present, then retrieve the next batch of results from the preceding call to this method.
          page_token must be the value of next_page_token from the previous response.
          The values of other method parameters should be identical to those in the previous call.

definition.name: list_time_series
definition.description:
Use this as the primary tool to retrieve metric data over a specific time period.
    This is the core tool for monitoring and observability, allowing you to get the actual data points for a given metric.

name.description:
Required. The project, organization or folder on which to execute the request. The format is:
        projects/[PROJECT_ID_OR_NUMBER]
        organizations/[ORGANIZATION_ID]
        folders/[FOLDER_ID]

filter.description:
Required. A monitoring filter that specifies which time series should be returned.
        (https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/v3/filters#time-series-filter).
        Examples:
        - To get CPU usage:
            'metric.type = "compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/usage_time"'
        - To return all time series from a specific Compute Engine instance, use the following filter:
            'metric.type = "compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/usage_time" AND metric.labels.instance_name = "my-instance-name"'
        - To return all time series from Compute Engine instances whose names start with frontend-, use the following filter:
            'metric.type = "compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/usage_time" AND metric.labels.instance_name = starts_with("frontend-")'

startTime.description:
Optional. Start of the time interval (inclusive) during which the time series data was collected.
              Must be in RFC 3339 format.

endTime.description:
Required. End of the time interval (inclusive) during which the time series data was collected.
            Must be in RFC 3339 format.

interval.description:
Required. The time interval for which results should be returned.
        Only time series that contain data points in the specified interval are included in the response.

alignmentPeriod.description:
The alignmentPeriod specifies a time interval, in seconds, that is used to divide the data in all the time series into consistent blocks of time.
              The value must be at least 60 seconds.

perSeriesAligner.description:
An Aligner describes how to bring the data points in a single time series into temporal alignment.
              Except for ALIGN_NONE, all alignments cause all the data points in an alignmentPeriod to be mathematically grouped together, resulting in a single data point for each alignmentPeriod with end timestamp at the end of the period.

aggregation.description: Optional. Specifies the alignment of data points in individual time series. By default (if no aggregation is explicitly specified), the raw time series data is returned.

pageSize.description: Optional. A positive number that is the maximum number of results to return.

pageToken.description: Optional. If this field is not empty then it must contain the nextPageToken value returned by a previous call to this method.

definition.name: driver_session
definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Start/stop automation session to connect to a RUNNING Tauri app. Supports multiple concurrent app connections - each app runs on a unique port. The most recently connected app becomes the "default" app used when no appIdentifier is specified. Use action "status" to check connection state: returns single app format when 1 app connected, or array format with "isDefault" indicator when multiple apps connected. Action "stop" without appIdentifier stops ALL sessions; with appIdentifier stops only that app. The identifier field (e.g., "com.example.myapp") uniquely identifies each app. REQUIRED before using other webview_* or ipc_* tools. Connects via WebSocket to the MCP Bridge plugin in the Tauri app. For browser automation, use Chrome DevTools MCP instead. For Electron apps, this tool will NOT work.

action.description: Action to perform: start or stop the session, or check status

host.description: Host address to connect to (e.g., 192.168.1.100). Falls back to MCP_BRIDGE_HOST or TAURI_DEV_HOST env vars

appIdentifier.description: App identifier (port number or bundle ID) to stop. Only used with action "stop". If omitted, stops all sessions.

definition.name: get_setup_instructions
definition.description: Get instructions for setting up or updating the MCP Bridge plugin in a Tauri project. Call this tool when: (1) driver_session fails to connect, (2) you detect the plugin is not installed or outdated, or (3) the user asks about setup. Returns step-by-step guidance that you should follow to help the user configure their project. IMPORTANT: The instructions require you to examine the project first and ask for permission before making any changes.

definition.name: ipc_emit_event
definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Emit a Tauri event to test event handlers. Requires active driver_session. Events are Tauri-specific (not DOM events). For browser DOM events, use Chrome DevTools MCP instead.

appIdentifier.description: App port or bundle ID to target. Defaults to the only connected app or the default app if multiple are connected.

definition.name: ipc_execute_command
definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Execute Tauri IPC commands (invoke Rust backend functions). Requires active driver_session. This is Tauri-specific IPC, not browser APIs. Plugin commands (plugin:mcp-bridge|*) are routed through the bridge; all other commands are executed via the webview using window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke, which keeps the application's Tauri capability rules in force. For Electron IPC or browser APIs, use appropriate tools for those frameworks.

windowId.description: Window label to target (defaults to "main") for app commands

appIdentifier.description: App port or bundle ID to target. Defaults to the only connected app or the default app if multiple are connected.

definition.name: ipc_get_backend_state
definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Get Tauri backend state: app metadata, Tauri version, environment. Requires active driver_session. Use to verify you're connected to a Tauri app and get app info.

appIdentifier.description: App port or bundle ID to target. Defaults to the only connected app or the default app if multiple are connected.

definition.name: ipc_get_captured
definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Get captured Tauri IPC traffic (requires ipc_monitor started). Shows captured commands (invoke calls) and events with arguments and responses. For browser network requests, use Chrome DevTools MCP instead.

filter.description: Filter events by command name

appIdentifier.description: App port or bundle ID to target. Defaults to the only connected app or the default app if multiple are connected.

definition.name: ipc_monitor
definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Monitor Tauri IPC calls between frontend and Rust backend. Requires active driver_session. Captures invoke() calls made through window.__TAURI__.core. Bridge-internal commands (plugin:mcp-bridge|*) are excluded from capture. This is Tauri-specific; for browser network monitoring, use Chrome DevTools MCP.

action.description: Action to perform: start or stop IPC monitoring

appIdentifier.description: App port or bundle ID to target. Defaults to the only connected app or the default app if multiple are connected.

definition.name: list_devices
definition.description: [Tauri Mobile Apps Only] List Android emulators/devices and iOS simulators. Use for Tauri mobile development (tauri android dev, tauri ios dev). Not needed for desktop-only Tauri apps or web projects.

definition.name: manage_window
definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Manage Tauri windows. Actions: "list" - List all windows with labels, titles, URLs, and state. "info" - Get detailed info for a window (size, position, title, focus, visibility). "resize" - Resize a window (requires width/height, uses logical pixels by default). "focus" - Focus a window (bring to front). "minimize" - Minimize a window. "maximize" - Maximize a window. Desktop-only actions (focus, minimize, maximize) require tauri-plugin-mcp-bridge 0.13.0+ and return a version error on older plugins. Requires active driver_session. For browser windows, use Chrome DevTools MCP instead.

action.description: Action: "list" all windows, get "info" for one window, "resize" a window, "focus" a window, "minimize" a window, or "maximize" a window

windowId.description: Window label to target (defaults to "main"). Required for "info", optional for "resize", "focus", "minimize", "maximize"

logical.description: Use logical pixels (true, default) or physical pixels (false). Only for "resize"

appIdentifier.description: App port or bundle ID to target. Defaults to the only connected app or the default app if multiple are connected.

definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Read logs from various sources: "console" for webview JS logs, "android" for logcat, "ios" for simulator logs, "system" for desktop logs. Requires active driver_session for console logs. Use for debugging Tauri app issues at any level.

source.description: Log source: "console" for webview JS logs, "android" for logcat, "ios" for simulator, "system" for desktop

level.description: Only return entries at this console level.

maxChars.description: Maximum characters in the response. Entries are truncated and the oldest are dropped to fit.

maxCharsPerEntry.description: Maximum characters kept from each log entry.

filter.description: Regex or keyword to filter logs

since.description: ISO timestamp to filter logs since (e.g. 2023-10-27T10:00:00Z)

windowId.description: Window label for console logs (defaults to "main")

definition.name: webview_dom_snapshot
definition.description: [Tauri Apps Only] Get a structured DOM snapshot of a Tauri app's webview. Supports different snapshot types for AI consumption. The "accessibility" type returns a YAML representation of the accessibility tree similar to Playwright's aria snapshots, including roles, names, states, and element refs. Use this for understanding UI semantics, finding interactive elements, or accessibility testing. The "structure" type returns a YAML representation of the DOM hierarchy with element tag names, IDs, CSS classes, and data-testid attributes (if present). definition.name: mcp__C2d
definition.description:
使用此工具将代码文件发送到 MasterGo MCP 服务进行 C2D（代码转设计）处理，将用户代码同步到设计稿。

参数说明：
- filePath：HTML 文件的完整路径（如 /path/to/file.html），工具会自动读取文件内容并发送给后端。
- fileId： 不提供 shortLink 时至少需要 fileId。layerId 不是必填，没有就不要传。
- layerId： 可选。图层 ID（只读取 URL 参数 layer_id）。不传或解析不到则仅按 file 维度同步；pageid/page_id 不会被当作 layerId。
- shortLink：可选，短链接形式（例如 https://{domain}/goto/xxxx）。
  注意事项：只允许使用 URL 中的 layer_id 参数作为 layerId，严禁将 pageid/page_id 等任何页面 ID 当作 layerId。
  如果短链接或 URL 中没有解析出 layer_id，则不传 layerId。

工具会读取 filePath 指定文件的内容，并传给后端，附带 fileId 与可选的 layerId。

filePath.description: HTML 文件的完整路径，工具会读取文件内容并发送给后端

fileId.description: 文件 ID（URL 中 file= 或路径中的数字段）。未传 shortLink 时必填。

layerId.description: 可选。图层 ID（只读取 URL 参数 layer_id）。不传或解析不到则仅按 file 维度同步；pageid/page_id 不会被当作 layerId。

definition.name: mcp__applyDesign
definition.description:
Finalize generated design code: replace ALL placeholders (SVG icons + long text) with real high-precision data from the design cache, then write the final file directly to disk. WHAT it does: 1. Replaces every `@@SVG:{svgShortKey}@@` placeholder with the real high-precision `@@SVG:S0#0@@ - Long text: `T{sectionIndex}|{nodeId}` — appears in TEXT nodes whose text was too long for inline DSL. Example:

T3|1:1234:5678

The server escapes the injected data according to the `targetLang` parameter: - `html` (default, also for Vue templates): place the placeholder in element content (`@@SVG:S0#0@@`, `

T3|1:2

`). SVG is inserted as-is; long text is HTML-escaped (& < >). - `dart` (Flutter): place the placeholder inside a single-quoted string literal (`SvgPicture.string('@@SVG:S0#0@@')`, `Text('T3|1:2')`). SVG/text are escaped for that string (\ ' newline). Pass `targetLang: "dart"`. Pick targetLang to match the code you generated, and place placeholders in that language's standard position shown above. You can provide either: 1. fileId and layerId directly, or 2. a short link (like https://{domain}/goto/LhGgBAK) IMPORTANT: Call this tool with the COMPLETE code string. After the tool writes the file, you are DONE — do NOT output or edit the code further.

fileId.description: MasterGo design file ID. Required if shortLink is not provided. Must match the fileId used in getDesignSections.

layerId.description: Root layer ID of the design. Required if shortLink is not provided. Must match the layerId used in getDesignSections.

sourceLayerId.description: Source layer ID from URL parameter source_layer_id. When provided, use this instead of layerId for all queries.

code.description: The COMPLETE generated code containing @@SVG:{svgShortKey}@@ and/or T{sectionIndex}|{nodeId} placeholders.

outDir.description: Output directory where the final file will be written. The finalized code (with all placeholders replaced by real data) is written directly to this directory — do NOT re-output or edit the code after this tool runs. Example: '/Users/you/project/output' or './output'.

outputFileName.description: Output file name (default: 'index.html'). Include extension. Example: 'snmp-agent.html'.

targetLang.description: Target language of the generated code, decides placeholder escaping. 'html' (default, also for Vue): SVG inserted as-is into element content, long text HTML-escaped. 'dart' (Flutter): SVG/text escaped for single-quoted string literals (SvgPicture.string('...'), Text('...')).

definition.name: mcp__downloadExportAssets
definition.description:
Download the REAL slice images (切图) that the designer configured on a MasterGo design,
and save them as local image files.

WHY THIS TOOL EXISTS
Rendering a slice produces image bytes on the **SERVER's** disk — a `filePath` you cannot open
from your machine. This tool fetches those bytes over HTTP and writes them into YOUR local output
directory, returning paths you can actually use.

WHEN TO USE
- You need the actual PNG / JPG / WEBP slice files to reference in generated code.
- `mcp__getExportList` told you which nodes are slices (nodes with Export settings).
  Slices MUST be restored as ONE whole image — never decomposed into child layers.

WHAT IT RETURNS
- `assets[]`: { exportId, layerId, fileName, format, bytes, filePath } — files actually written locally
- `skipped[]`: { exportId, reason } — slices that could not be fetched
- `dir`: the directory the files were written to
- `autoRendered`: true when this call had to render the slices first (nothing was cached yet)

HOW IT WORKS (fully automatic — ONE call is enough)
1. Reads the server's cached slice list for this file/layer.
2. If nothing is cached, it **renders the slices automatically** (no extra call needed from you).
3. Downloads each slice and writes it to `outDir`.

WHY THAT MATTERS
The server caches rendered slice bytes in memory (TTL ~5 minutes). If you call this tool long after
a previous render, the cache may have expired — this tool re-renders on demand instead of failing.

SCOPE SEMANTICS
Scope = the subtree of the `layerId` you pass. Use the SAME layerId you are restoring: a container
returns the slices inside its subtree, a page id returns every slice on that page. A node that is
ITSELF a slice is NOT part of its own subtree, so passing that node's own id will not return it —
pass its PARENT container's id (the scope you are restoring), or the page id when restoring the
whole page.
A nearly-empty result on a page id does NOT prove the design has no slices: some documents return a
minimal page chunk while slice settings live in layer scope. Query the layer you are restoring.

WHAT "NO SLICE" MEANS
If the design genuinely has no Export settings in scope, this tool says so explicitly — in that case
restore the nodes as normal layers (from the DSL), do NOT invent images.

LIMITATIONS
- Only PNG / JPG / WEBP are produced server-side (SVG / PDF / AVIF are not).
- Slices attached to layers INSIDE a component instance are skipped by the renderer.
- At most 20 slices per underlying render call.

fileId.description: MasterGo design file ID (format: file/<fileId> in MasterGo URL). Required if shortLink is not provided.

layerId.description: Layer id (container / node) OR page id — same semantics as mcp__getExportList. A slice node does not include itself in its own subtree scope; use the page id to find slices.

sourceLayerId.description: Source layer ID from URL parameter source_layer_id. When provided, use this instead of layerId.

exportIds.description: Only download these export settings ids. Omit to download every cached slice in scope.

outDir.description: Output directory for the slice image files. Relative paths resolve against MG_OUTPUT_ROOT (default: current working directory). Omit to use the current working directory.

format.description:
Output format for design data. Defaults to json.
- json — default; useful when piping output into tools that expect JSON.
- yaml — fewer tokens than JSON for typical designs.
- tree — experimental compact format. Structural keys (id, name, type) are encoded positionally on each node line, and style values stay deduplicated in a globalVars block. Designs with heavy style reuse see the largest token savings.

definition.name: mcp__extractSvg
definition.description:
Extract SVG data from MasterGo design files. This tool retrieves the DSL from a design layer, finds all PATH nodes (typically inside INSTANCE/icon components), resolves their color references, and generates SVG markup strings.
You can provide either:
1. fileId and layerId directly, or
2. a short link (like https://{domain}/goto/LhGgBAK)

Pagination: When there are many icons, use the first call without "page" to get totalCount. Then call again with page=0, page=1, etc. (page starts at 0, pageSize defaults to 20, max 100). If hasMore is false, you've fetched all pages.

fileId.description: MasterGo design file ID (format: file/<fileId> in MasterGo URL). Required if shortLink is not provided.

layerId.description: Layer ID of the specific component or element to retrieve (format: ?layer_id=<layerId>). Required if shortLink is not provided.

sourceLayerId.description: Source layer ID from URL parameter source_layer_id. When provided, use this instead of layerId for all queries.

backgroundColor.description: Solid background color for the SVG (e.g. '#000000', 'black'). Useful for previewing white/light icons.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 0). Omit to get all SVGs at once. When provided, the response includes totalCount/hasMore/page/pageSize for you to iterate through all pages.

pageSize.description: Number of SVGs per page (default 20, max 100). Only used when page is provided.

format.description:
Output format for design data. Defaults to json.
- json — default; useful when piping output into tools that expect JSON.
- yaml — fewer tokens than JSON for typical designs.
- tree — experimental compact format. Structural keys (id, name, type) are encoded positionally on each node line, and style values stay deduplicated in a globalVars block. Designs with heavy style reuse see the largest token savings.

definition.name: mcp__getDesignSections
definition.description:
BEFORE calling this tool, CHECK the layerId:
- If a previous call returned error code [10017] (layer exceeds the 20MB limit), do NOT retry that
  same layerId and do NOT fall back to mcp__getDsl — it fetches the same oversized data.
  Use the page_id from the URL with mcp__getPageLayers to enumerate top-level layers, then restore
  them one by one. If one top-level layer is still too large, ask the user to select a smaller
  nested container in the MasterGo canvas and copy its link.
- If layerId has NO colon and no digits (e.g. "M", or any short non-numeric id), it is likely a
  PAGE-level id, NOT a layer id. Page-level ids return EMPTY from this tool (they cannot be
  enumerated via /container).
  → STOP. Call mcp__getPageLayers with the same fileId+layerId first to enumerate the real
  layer_ids, then restore each one individually.
- Only proceed with THIS tool when layerId looks like a real layer id (contains a colon and
  digits, e.g. "802:02364", "453:6855").
This check is MANDATORY when the user's URL contains ?page_id= (not ?layer_id=). If you ignore
this and call this tool with a page-level id, the server will return an error redirecting you to
mcp__getPageLayers anyway — so save the round-trip and call getPageLayers first.

[PRIMARY] This is the main tool for all designs. Operates in TWO modes:

Mode 1 — Get layout overview (sectionIndex NOT provided):
Returns the list of all sections with id, name, type, nodeCount, textPreview (first TEXT node, 20 chars max), and a page-absolute bounding box (x, y, width, height) for each section, plus totalSections and totalNodes.
Also returns rootMetadata (root layer width/height/name/type/fill) when available. rootContainer CSS properties for the page wrapper. splitContainers for large page regions that were split into child sections.
Use this FIRST to understand the design scope. The per-section bbox tells you exactly where each section sits inside the root container — use it for absolute positioning when generating code.
Example: { "fileId": "123", "layerId": "456:789" }

Mode 2 — Get section DSL (sectionIndex provided):
Returns the full DSL for ONE specific section.
- PATH nodes carry a `svgShortKey` field (a short sequential ID like `S0#0`, `S0#1`). The SVG markup is NOT in the DSL. Place `@@SVG:{svgShortKey}@@` where each icon goes, then call `mcp__applyDesign` at the end to inject the real high-precision SVG. NEVER hand-write `<path d="...">`.
- CRITICAL: After generating the complete code with all `@@SVG:{svgShortKey}@@` placeholders, call `mcp__applyDesign` to replace them with real SVG. Skipping this WILL cause missing icons.
- INSTANCE nodes with a `_variantProps` object carry semantic state labels. Compare these across sibling instances to determine active/selected/hovered states — do NOT default to the first item.

CRITICAL — sectionIndex is SINGULAR: the parameter is sectionIndex (a SINGLE integer per call). There is NO plural sectionIndices parameter — passing an array will be rejected with an error. To fetch multiple sections you MUST make multiple calls, each with one sectionIndex.

IMPORTANT workflow:
1. First call WITHOUT sectionIndex to get the section list with node counts.
2. Then call WITH sectionIndex=0, then sectionIndex=1, ... up to totalSections-1 — ONE sectionIndex per call.
3. YOU MUST REQUEST ALL SECTIONS. Do NOT skip any section index — missing sections WILL cause missing content.
4. textPreview helps distinguish same-looking sections: "系统信息", "权限设置", "基本设置" — all may have nodeCount=3 and empty name but DIFFERENT textPreview. They are individual menu items, NOT duplicates.
5. Fetch sections in batches of 3-5 CONCURRENT calls (3-5 separate single-sectionIndex calls in parallel), wait for all results, then send the next batch. Each call has exactly one sectionIndex.
6. After fetching all sections, generate code with `@@SVG:{svgShortKey}@@` placeholders for every PATH node, then call `mcp__applyDesign` to inject real SVG.
7. Count your requests. If totalSections=48, you must make exactly 48 sectionIndex calls (each with a SINGLE integer). Keep a checklist and do NOT stop early.
8. Generate the complete HTML with all SVG placeholders, then call `mcp__applyDesign` as the FINAL step.

DO NOT call mcp__getDsl after completing this workflow — all data is already provided.
If this tool is unavailable on an old server (HTTP 404), fall back to mcp__getDsl. For error code
[10017], do NOT fall back to getDsl — follow the OVERSIZED LAYER instructions above. For other
errors (e.g. HTTP 5xx or network timeout), retry once; if it still fails, fall back to mcp__getDsl
or report the error to the user.

You can provide either:
1. fileId and layerId directly, or
2. a short link (like https://{domain}/goto/LhGgBAK)

definition.name: mcp__getExportList
definition.description:
List the Export (切图) settings configured on a MasterGo design, WITHOUT rendering any image.
This is the CHEAP metadata step — it only reads the design's Export configuration.

WHY YOU NEED THIS
Some nodes are marked by the designer as **slices** (切图). Those nodes must be restored as
ONE whole image block — NOT decomposed into their child layers, and NOT hand-drawn. But you
cannot know which nodes those are from the ordinary DSL, because the DSL does not carry Export
settings. This tool tells you exactly which nodes are slices.

WHEN TO USE
- Before restoring a design, to learn whether any node is a slice.
- When the user asks for exported assets / 切图 / @2x PNG of a specific area.
- Before calling `mcp__downloadExportAssets` (which needs to know which slices exist).

WHAT YOU GET BACK
- `exports[]`: { id, layerId, layerName, layerType, format, sizeRule, sizeValue,
                   targetWidth, targetHeight, exportQuality, isSuffix, isBKVisible, ... }
  - `id` is the export setting id — pass this as `exportIds` when rendering/downloading.
  - `layerId` is the node that carries the slice (different from `id`).
  - `targetWidth` / `targetHeight` are the OUTPUT pixel size the designer configured.
- `scope`: "page" or "layer" — tells you what range was resolved.
- `skipped`: counts of referenced layers that are missing / removed from this design.
- `imageRefs`: image references inside slice subtrees (used by the renderer to carry bitmaps).
- `total`: number of slices in scope. `total: 0` means no slices — restore everything as layers.
- `guidance`: how to treat the found slices when generating code.

SCOPE SEMANTICS (important)
The scope is the subtree of the layerId you pass:
- `layerId = the container/node you are restoring` → the slices inside its subtree (preferred:
  same scope you feed into the section workflow).
- `layerId = page_id` (e.g. "M") → all slices in that page (use when restoring the whole page).
  A nearly-empty page chunk does NOT prove the design has no slices: some documents return a
  minimal page document while slice settings live in layer scope.
  A node that is ITSELF a slice is NOT included in its own subtree scope — pass its parent
  container's id (or the page id) to find that node. This is why asking with the slice node's own
  id can return 0.

NOTE: the section LIST response already carries a `slices` summary for the restore scope.
Check that field first; call this tool when it is absent (older server) or you need the full
export configuration (scale rule / quality / export id for downloading).

SUPPORTED FORMATS
PNG / JPG / WEBP can be rendered server-side. SVG / PDF / AVIF appear in the list but cannot be
rendered by the downstream export endpoint — report that honestly instead of pretending.

fileId.description: MasterGo design file ID (format: file/<fileId> in MasterGo URL). Required if shortLink is not provided.

layerId.description: Layer id (container / node) OR page id. Scope = that node's subtree; a slice node does NOT include itself — use the page id to find it.

sourceLayerId.description: Source layer ID from URL parameter source_layer_id. When provided, use this instead of layerId.

definition.name: mcp__getPageLayers
definition.description:
List ALL layers under a given page (or any container layer) of a MasterGo design file.
This is the ENUMERATION step of the multi-layer restoration workflow — it only lists
layer_ids; it does NOT restore designs.

**Workflow (enumerate → build URLs → restore one by one):**
  1. Call this tool with the page_id / parent layerId to get the full layer list.
  2. Pick the top-level restorable layers from the result (FRAME/COMPONENT/INSTANCE at
     depth 0/1). For each, build a URL: https://mastergo.com/file/{fileId}?layer_id={id}
     (URL-encode the id, e.g. 802:02364 → 802%3A02364).
  3. Restore them SEQUENTIALLY — take one layer_id, run the full single-layer restoration
     (mcp__getDesignSections → fetch all sections → mcp__applyDesign), write its HTML to its
     OWN separate .html file (a complete standalone document with <!DOCTYPE html>/<head>/<body>),
     THEN move to the next. Do NOT batch-restore. Do NOT merge multiple layers into one HTML file —
     ONE layer = ONE standalone .html file.

  AUTOMATED PROGRESS TRACKING: once this tool returns layers, a page restore plan is created
  automatically. Every subsequent getDesignSections response carries a `pageRestore` position,
  and every applyDesign success response carries `pageRestore.next` with the NEXT layer to
  restore (layerId + suggested file name). Follow those fields instead of tracking manually —
  they are the authoritative progress record for the whole page.

OVERSIZED PARENT LAYER (a previous call to getDesignSections/getDsl/getMeta returned error
code [10017] "layer data exceeds the 20MB limit"):
Do NOT pass the same oversized container layerId to this tool — that downloads the same layer data
and hits the same limit. Use the page-level ID from the URL (page_id) to list that page's top-level
layers, then restore them individually via getDesignSections. If a top-level layer is still too
large, ask the user to select a smaller nested container in the MasterGo canvas and copy its link.

You can provide either:
1. fileId and layerId directly (layerId = the page's layerId, i.e. page_id), or
2. a short link (like https://{domain}/goto/LhGgBAK)

The returned layer list is lightweight: each entry has id, name, type, depth, parentId,
childrenCount, width, height. It does NOT contain DSL/styles/SVG paths — use the section
or DSL tools to restore each layer.

NOTE: This tool cannot enumerate a document's PAGE list from a fileId alone — you must
already know a page_id / layerId to pass in.

The URL marker `page_id=M` means the file's DEFAULT page and IS supported — do NOT ask the
user for "a real layer_id URL" just because the page_id is `M`.

EMPTY RESULT — TWO DISTINCT CASES (must distinguish):
1. **Page genuinely has no layers** (`totalLayers: 0` + `pageName` present + NO `needsCanvasVisit`):
   the page EXISTS in this file but contains no restorable layers. This is a real empty page —
   do NOT tell the user to visit the canvas; report it as an empty page.
2. **Page not found / data unavailable** (`needsCanvasVisit: true` + `guidance` field present):
   the page_id is not a page of this file (e.g. it is a container/layer id, or the page was deleted),
   OR the page data could not be loaded (too large / timeout). Relay the `guidance` text to the user.
Do NOT silently treat an empty result without checking which case it is.

fileId.description: MasterGo design file ID (format: file/<fileId> in MasterGo URL). Required if shortLink is not provided.

layerId.description: Page layer ID to enumerate. This is the page_id from the MasterGo URL (e.g. "40:015"). Required if shortLink is not provided.

definition.name: meshy_analyze_printability
definition.title: Analyze Model Printability
definition.description:
Check whether a model is printable: watertightness, non-manifold edges, holes, degenerate faces and volume — plus thin walls when printer_type and/or a print size is given (FDM, SLA/resin or full-color). FREE. This is the authoritative answer to "is it printable?".

The finished task (task_type "print-analyze") reports printability.status:
  - error → meshy_repair_printability (pass this analyze task as input_task_id to reuse its printer and size)
  - warning → repair is optional
  - healthy → download the analyzed source task's model (the analyze task has none)

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", printer_type: "sla", intended_print_height_mm: 100 }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, remesh or retexture task on Meshy 6 or newer, or a print-repair task. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB).

printer_type.description: Sets the minimum wall: fdm 1.0 mm, sla 0.8 mm, full_color 2.0 mm (fdm when only a size is sent). Without a size: 150 mm tall for GLB / tasks, an STL's own size, else 150 mm longest side.

intended_print_height_mm.description: Print height in mm (1–1000); GLB / input_task_id only. At most one print size.

intended_print_longest_side_mm.description: Print's longest side in mm (1–1000); any format. At most one print size.

definition.name: meshy_auto_split
definition.title: Auto Split Model into Printable Parts
definition.description:
Cut a model into separately printable parts: when it is too big for the bed, parts need different colors/materials, or it should be assembled. Cost: 10 credits. The texture is not kept.

There is no bed-size parameter: cuts follow mode and prompt, not your printer, so resize the model to the print size first (meshy_resize) when parts must fit a bed, then check the part sizes and re-split by_parts if one is still too big.
Then meshy_download_model (3mf if requested) and meshy_send_to_slicer.

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", mode: "by_parts", prompt: "the figure and the base", target_formats: ["3mf"], connectors: true }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-3d preview, remesh, convert or resize task made with meshy-6, meshy-7, meshy-7.1 or latest (not low-poly or Smart Topology).

mode.description: 'auto' (default; Meshy picks the cuts), 'by_parts' (the parts named in prompt), or 'by_color' (the color regions named in prompt; image-to-3d / multi-image-to-3d sources only).

prompt.description: Required for by_parts / by_color: name 1–10 parts, e.g. 'head, torso, arms, legs'; the rest becomes one more part. If unreadable, the task falls back to auto, still charges, and reports prompt_ignored.

target_formats.description: Extra formats (glb is always made). 3mf gives separately selectable parts in a slicer; stl fuses them into one solid.

layout.description: 'assembled' (default) or 'on_plate' (parts laid flat, ready to slice).

connectors.description: Add mortise-and-tenon connectors at each cut so the parts fit together.

definition.name: meshy_cancel_task
definition.title: Cancel or Delete Task
definition.description:
Cancel a queued task, or delete a finished one. What happens depends on the task:

Creative Lab tasks (task_type "creative-lab-..."):
  - PENDING → canceled, credits refunded
  - IN_PROGRESS → canceled, credits NOT refunded
  - SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELED → cannot be canceled or deleted, even with confirm_delete

Every other task:
  - PENDING → deleted, credits refunded
  - IN_PROGRESS → refused: the task keeps running and its credits are not refundable. Wait until it finishes
  - SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELED → PERMANENTLY deleted with its files, no refund. Requires confirm_delete: true — ask the user first

Returns { success, task_id, task_type, previous_status, message }.

task_type.description: Optional: if omitted or wrong, the server finds the task and reports its real type.

confirm_delete.description: true to permanently delete a finished task, only after the user agreed.
