definition.name: append_file
definition.title: Append File
definition.description: Append text to the end of a file, creating the file if it does not exist. The existing content is never changed or replaced. The text is appended exactly as given, with no newline added before or after it, so end it with a newline if the next append should start on a new line. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file to append to; it is created if it does not exist. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

content.description: Text to append, exactly as given. No newline is added: end it with \n if the next append should start on a new line.

definition.name: copy_file
definition.title: Copy File
definition.description: Copy a file to a new location, without reading its content into the conversation. Copies one regular file, keeping its permissions and modification time; directories are not copied. If the destination exists, the operation will fail: it never overwrites. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

source.description: The file to copy

destination.description: Where to create the copy; nothing may exist there yet

definition.name: create_directory
definition.title: Create Directory
definition.description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to create, with any missing parents; an existing directory is left as is. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

definition.name: directory_tree
definition.title: Directory Tree
definition.description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty), except at the last level when 'depth' limits the tree: those directories are not read and have no children array. The output is formatted with 2-space indentation for readability. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory at the root of the tree. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

excludePatterns.description: Patterns for entries to leave out, with their contents, matched against each entry's path relative to path. A pattern with no '*' matches that name at any depth ('node_modules' leaves out every node_modules directory); a pattern with '*' is a glob matched as written, and one ending in '/**' also leaves out the directory it names.

depth.description: How many levels to descend: 1 lists only the entries directly in path. Directories at the last level have no children array. Omit for the whole tree.

definition.name: edit_file
definition.title: Edit File
definition.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Edits apply in order, each to the result of the ones before it, and each replaces the first match of its oldText with newText. oldText must match the file's text exactly, except that line endings (LF or CRLF) never matter and, when there is no exact match, a run of whole lines matches if each line is equal once leading and trailing whitespace is ignored (newText then takes the file's indentation). Whitespace inside a line must match. If any edit has no match, nothing is written and the error shows the closest lines of the file, numbered, to copy oldText from. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The text file to edit. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

edits.description: The replacements to make, applied in order, each to the result of the ones before it. If any one has no match, none is written.

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format

definition.name: get_file_info
definition.title: Get File Info
definition.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, type and hard-link count. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file or directory to describe. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

definition.name: list_allowed_directories
definition.title: List Allowed Directories
definition.description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.

definition.name: list_directory
definition.title: List Directory
definition.description: List the files and directories directly inside a path, each marked [FILE] or [DIR]. Use it to see what a directory contains; when you also need each entry's size or want entries sorted by size, use list_directory_with_sizes instead, and for a recursive view use directory_tree. Returns one line per entry. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to list. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

definition.name: list_directory_with_sizes
definition.title: List Directory with Sizes
definition.description: List the files and directories directly inside a path with each file's size, marked [FILE] or [DIR], sorted by name or by size, largest first (sortBy). Use it when sizes matter, such as finding the largest files; for names only, use list_directory, which returns less text. Returns one line per entry, followed by the totals. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to list. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

sortBy.description: Sort entries by name or size

definition.name: move_file
definition.title: Move File
definition.description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

source.description: The file or directory to move or rename. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

destination.description: Its new path, including the name; nothing may exist there yet. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

definition.name: read_file
definition.title: Read File (Deprecated)
definition.description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.

path.description: The file to read as text. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

definition.name: read_media_file
definition.title: Read Media File
definition.description: Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. Image and audio files are returned as image/audio content; any other file type is returned as an embedded resource. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The image, audio or other file to read as base64. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

definition.name: read_multiple_files
definition.title: Read Multiple Files
definition.description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. Only works within allowed directories.

paths.description: Array of file paths to read. Each path must be a string pointing to a valid file within allowed directories.

definition.name: read_text_file
definition.title: Read Text File
definition.description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file. Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines of a file, or the 'tail' parameter to read only the last N lines of a file. Operates on the file as text regardless of extension. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file to read as text. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

definition.name: search_files
definition.title: Search Files
definition.description: Find files and directories by NAME, not by content: this tool never reads or searches inside files. It walks the tree under 'path' and matches a glob pattern against each entry's path relative to 'path' (case-sensitive). Use '*.ext' to match entries directly under 'path', and '**/*.ext' or '**/name' to match at any depth. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding files when you don't know their exact location. Only searches within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to search under. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

pattern.description: Glob matched against each entry's path relative to path, never its content: '*.ts' matches directly under path, '**/*.ts' at any depth.

excludePatterns.description: Patterns for entries to leave out, with their contents, matched against each entry's path relative to path. A pattern with no '*' matches that name at any depth ('node_modules' leaves out every node_modules directory); a pattern with '*' is a glob matched as written, and one ending in '/**' also leaves out the directory it names.

definition.name: write_file
definition.title: Write File
definition.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file to create, or to overwrite if it exists; its parent directory must exist. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

content.description: The complete text the file will contain, replacing any it had

resource_templates.name: file
resource_templates.title: File
resource_templates.description: A file inside the allowed directories, by its absolute file:// URI (for example file:///home/user/project/README.md). Text files are returned as text, other files as a base64 blob with their MIME type. Directories are not resources; use the list_directory tool to find files.

definition.name: add_observations
definition.title: Add Observations
definition.description: Add new observations to existing entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity to add the observations to

contents.description: An array of observation contents to add

observations.description: The observations to add, grouped by entity. Each entity must already exist; an observation it already has is not added again

definition.name: create_entities
definition.title: Create Entities
definition.description: Create multiple new entities in the knowledge graph. An entity whose name already exists, or repeats an earlier entity in the same call, is skipped and its observations are not added; the result lists the skipped names in `skipped`. Use add_observations to add observations to an existing entity.

name.description: The name of the entity

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

entities.description: The entities to create, each with a name unique in the graph

name.description: The name of the entity

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

definition.name: create_relations
definition.title: Create Relations
definition.description: Create multiple new relations between entities in the knowledge graph. Relations should be in active voice

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

relations.description: The relations to create. Both ends must name existing entities; a relation already in the graph is not added again

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

definition.name: delete_entities
definition.title: Delete Entities
definition.description: Delete whole entities from the knowledge graph, together with every relation that points to or from them and all their observations. Use it only to remove an entity entirely; to remove a link between two entities and keep both, use delete_relations, and to remove facts from an entity, use delete_observations. Cannot be undone.

entityNames.description: An array of entity names to delete

definition.name: delete_observations
definition.title: Delete Observations
definition.description: Delete specific observations from entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity containing the observations

observations.description: An array of observations to delete

deletions.description: The observations to delete, grouped by entity, each matched by its exact text

definition.name: delete_relations
definition.title: Delete Relations
definition.description: Delete specific relations (from, to, relationType) from the knowledge graph and keep the entities they connect. Each relation must match an existing one exactly on all three fields; if unsure, call open_nodes (or search_nodes) first to read the stored relationType. Use it to remove a link between two entities; to remove an entity itself, use delete_entities. Cannot be undone.

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

relations.description: An array of relations to delete

definition.name: open_nodes
definition.title: Open Nodes
definition.description: Retrieve specific entities by their exact names, with every relation that touches one of them. Use this when you already know the names (from the conversation, or from an earlier search_nodes or read_graph result); it is the cheapest way to read entities you can name. Prefer search_nodes when you only have a keyword or part of a name. Names that do not exist are skipped.

names.description: An array of entity names to retrieve

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

name.description: The name of the entity

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

observationCount.description: How many observations the entity holds in total; present only when observationLimit was given

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

definition.name: read_graph
definition.title: Read Graph
definition.description: Read the entire knowledge graph: every entity with its observations, and every relation. The result grows with the graph, so use this only when you need everything; prefer search_nodes to find entities by keyword and open_nodes to read entities whose names you know.

entityTypes.description: Return only entities whose entityType is one of these (exact match), and only the relations that touch one of them. Omit to return every entity.

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

name.description: The name of the entity

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

observationCount.description: How many observations the entity holds in total; present only when observationLimit was given

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

definition.name: search_nodes
definition.title: Search Nodes
definition.description: Search the knowledge graph for entities whose name, type or observations contain the query (case-insensitive). Use this when you have a keyword, a topic or part of a name but not the exact entity names. Prefer open_nodes when you already know the exact names, and use read_graph only when you need the whole graph. Returns the matching entities and every relation that touches one of them.

query.description: The search query to match against entity names, types, and observation content

limit.description: Return at most this many matching entities (the first matches, in stored order), with the relations that touch them. Omit to return every match.

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

name.description: The name of the entity

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

observationCount.description: How many observations the entity holds in total; present only when observationLimit was given

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

definition.name: sequentialthinking
definition.title: Sequential Thinking
definition.description:
A detailed tool for dynamic and reflective problem-solving through thoughts.
Each thought can build on, question, or revise previous insights as understanding deepens.

When to use this tool:
- Breaking down complex problems into steps
- Planning and design with room for revision
- Analysis that might need course correction
- Problems where the full scope might not be clear initially
- Tasks that need to maintain context over multiple steps
- Situations where irrelevant information needs to be filtered out

You should:
1. Estimate totalThoughts up front and adjust it up or down as you go; thoughtNumber may exceed it
2. Question or revise earlier thoughts (isRevision with revisesThought), or branch (branchFromThought with branchId)
3. Express uncertainty, and ignore information irrelevant to the current step
4. Generate a solution hypothesis, verify it against the earlier steps, and repeat until satisfied
5. Set nextThoughtNeeded to false only when truly done and a satisfactory answer is reached

nextThoughtNeeded.description: Whether another thought step is needed

totalThoughts.description: Estimated total thoughts needed (numeric value, e.g., 5, 10)

name.description: Track name
