definition.name: scroll
definition.description: Scroll in a direction, or toward the top/bottom edge of scrollable content. Set until to a selector to reach an off-screen target in one command rather than a scroll-and-check loop. The optional amount is the finger-path fraction of the viewport axis, honored up to 0.8 of it; directional scrolls reduce release momentum, while app scroll physics determine the final content offset. A visible keyboard shortens the swiped band instead of being dismissed; when too little is left, the command refuses with scroll_keyboard_occludes_surface. A directional scroll also reports the movement it observed as movement: moved, at-edge, unchanged, or unobserved when the two reads could not back a claim either way; an unchanged surface inside a container that still hides content in that direction refuses with scroll_no_progress rather than repeating the requested distance. The movement field is absent where a tier verifies per pass (top/bottom, until), where the runtime cannot read a screen, where a settle observation or a replay already owns that observation, or where the operator opted out of it. Times out after 90s; a caller-supplied budget extends it.

definition.name: agent_configure
definition.description: 起動済みのClaude／Codex／Grok／Cursor／Antigravity agent sessionを再起動せず、会話contextを保ったままmodel／reasoning effort／fastを変更する。各harnessのCLI標準model操作を使う。Cursorのreasoning_effort変更はmodelと同時指定する。Claude Codeの席では /model の選ぶ画面の「この会話だけ」（s）で替え、端末の ~/.claude/settings.json の既定は書き換えない。その選び方が無い版、選ぶ画面に無いmodel、そのmodelで選べないeffortは、何も変えずに断る。fastだけの指定も受ける。ファスト（harnessの高速の応答。費用や利用量が増える）。席は必ず通常の速度で起きる。trueはその席をfastへ切り替え、falseは通常の速度にする（fastに対応していないmodelでもfalseは受ける）。切り替えは席だけに留め、harnessが利用者の既定へ書いた分は切り替えの直前の値へ戻す。断りは文の先頭の符号で分かる: FAST_MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED（そのmodelは対応していない）、FAST_MODE_UNAVAILABLE（アカウントや契約で使えない）、FAST_MODE_MODEL_CONFLICT（modelへfast版のIDを書いてfalseを渡した）、FAST_MODE_UNCONFIRMED（切り替えた後の状態を確かめられない）。

definition.name: agent_launch
definition.description: エージェントを単一の標準入口から永続sessionへ起動する。harnessはagent loop・認証・hook・transcriptを所有する実行基盤、modelはそのharnessが選ぶ推論モデルであり別軸。Cursor harnessからGPT／Claude／Grok等を選んでも完了相関はCursor方式のまま。ComposerはCursorのmodelの一つで、harnessでもGrokのmodelでもない。harness=cursor-cli と model=composer-2.5-fast（またはcomposer-2.5）で指定する。remoteを付けると、SSHで入った別端末のAitermで同じ起動を行い、完了は同じ形で親へ届く。通常CLIと同じHOME・cwd・project/user/local設定・MCP・plugin・skill・permission/trustを共有する。aitermは完了相関stateだけをlaunch単位で所有する。起動されたagentにはsub-agent自己認識、親session、delegation depth/lineage、delegation_allowed=trueを注入し、必要な追加委譲は許可する。別のcomputer（登録済みの端末）で起こす時は、この起動にterminal（端末の登録元が渡す値をそのまま）とcwd（その端末のproject folder）を付ける。ここで起こしてからcd・sshしない。秘密の値はどの引数・prompt・送信文にも書かず、env_varsに名前だけを書く。dispatch した子は投げっぱなしでよい＝親はここで待たない。Codex親とClaude Code親にはAitermが回答本文を自動配送する。parent_deliveryがある場合はwait起動も通常の回答回収も不要。親は作業を続けるかターンを終える。Cursor親にはparent_deliveryとwait_processが付く。作業を続ければ次のツール返りに回答が差し込まれ、ターンを終える前にwait_processを背景で起動するとidle中の完了でも起きられる。ポーリングとpty_read(agent_transcript:true)は不要。その他の親では、完了通知をreceiptの `wait_process.executable` と `wait_process.args` をそのまま親のターンを塞がない別プロセスAPIへ渡して受け、PowerShell 7のStart-Processだけは `windows_start_process_argument_list` を単一文字列として渡す。exit を完了通知として扱う（exit 0=done / 3=timeout（既定600秒・未完了） / 4=closed / 7=error（harnessの記録でturnがAPIエラー等で打ち切られた。結果は無い）。receiptのoutcomeが正で、done以外は未完了。ポーリング不要）。`wait_command` は人間向け互換表示でありprocess境界へ使わない。foreground実行で親のターンを塞がない。自動配送以外の結果回収は pty_read(agent_transcript:true)。

terminal.description: Run this seat on another computer (a registered terminal) over SSH. Value: exactly the terminal value your host system's terminal registry hands over, {ref, target:{host,user,port}, os?, trustRevision, and credentialRevision or credential {handle, revision}}; copy it unchanged, never invent or edit it, never use a host name or ssh command instead. Omit it to launch on this computer. Give cwd in the same call: the absolute project folder on that terminal in its own form (a POSIX path starting with / on macOS and Linux, a drive path like C:\folder with backslashes on Windows). Never launch locally and then cd or ssh. Never put tokens, passwords or other secrets in any argument, prompt or typed text; pass secret values only by name in env_vars. After launch, use session_id alone for pty_send, pty_observe, pty_read, pty_key, claude_turn, agent_stop and pty_close; Aiterm routes them to the terminal. Errors and next step: TERMINAL_INVALID = malformed value, missing/relative cwd (or one in the other system's form), or combined with remote: pass the registry's value unchanged with cwd. TARGET_MISMATCH / BINDING_UNKNOWN = the value is not this terminal's binding: ask the terminal registry again. HOST_TRUST_STALE / CREDENTIAL_REVISION_STALE = the binding changed: get the current value from the terminal registry and launch again. HOST_KEY_MISMATCH / HOST_TRUST_MISSING = the terminal's host key is not the trusted one: the Owner must confirm the new host key; do not retry. CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED / CREDENTIAL_NOT_LOADED = this terminal's key comes from a credential handle that the registry must load first; never paste a key anywhere. AUTH_FAILED = the terminal refused the key. UNREACHABLE = the terminal is offline; try later. CONNECTION_REFUSED = the terminal refused the SSH connection (SSH may be off there); try later. REMOTE_AITERM_TOO_OLD = update Aiterm on the terminal. CWD_UNAVAILABLE = the folder does not exist there; do not pick another folder. SEAT_FORWARD_UNAVAILABLE = the seat's MCP route back to this computer is not ready (launch again later), or the seat MCP URLs are not http://127.0.0.1:<one port>/api/seat-mcp. All five harnesses run on a terminal; REMOTE_AITERM_TOO_OLD names the Aiterm version the harness needs there (claude-code 0.65.0, codex-cli 0.70.7, grok-cli / cursor-cli / antigravity-cli 0.70.9). TERMINAL_HARNESS_UNSUPPORTED = the harness name is none of the five. AGENT_LAUNCH_NOT_STARTED with _meta aiterm/launch_error code AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED = the CLI on the terminal is not logged in; the Owner logs it in there, then launch again. TERMINAL_OS_MISMATCH = the terminal is not the operating system os says: the registry's os is wrong or the binding points at another machine; ask the terminal registry, do not retry. TERMINAL_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED = the terminal is not a macOS, Linux or Windows system, so it cannot run seats.

append_system_prompt.description: Launch instructions added to the system prompt; kept in Aiterm state, not in the project or home. Never put secrets here. Codex: appended to developer_instructions after Aiterm's marker; Grok: appended to --rules; Antigravity: an always-on rule in the seat's own --add-dir folder; at most 64 KiB for these. Cursor has no system-prompt channel: the text goes in front of the first prompt, or of the first input sent to a promptless seat (at most 64 KiB)

mcp_config.description: Extra MCP servers for this seat. Secret header values: write ${NAME} and list NAME in env_vars. Codex, Grok, Cursor and Antigravity take only http servers {type?: "http", url, headers, replace?: boolean}: a literal header, 'Authorization: Bearer ${NAME}' or a header whose whole value is ${NAME}; other shapes, and a ${NAME} with no value at launch, are refused before the seat starts. A server the seat's own harness config already defines under the same name is dropped for this seat (listed in caller_mcp.dropped) unless its entry has replace: true; then it replaces that server (Codex: a user stdio server of that name runs Aiterm's relay to the given url instead). Cursor runs a server as plugin-aiterm-caller-<name> beside a same-name user server, so nothing is dropped there

fork_from.description: claude-code and codex-cli. Start a disposable fork of that seat's latest saved conversation, in its cwd, with the main's tools and MCP. Every write inside that cwd (the project folder) is refused below the tools for the whole process tree (Linux Landlock, macOS sandbox-exec, Windows restricted token + folder deny ACE); everything else is allowed. Requires a prompt; no write_scope. Close it after its answer

definition.name: claude_agent
definition.description: 【旧互換alias。新規連携は agent_launch(harness=claude-code)】Claude Codeの対話エージェントTUIを永続端末に起動する。`claude -p`ではなく、同じ利用者可視sessionへpty_sendで継続入力する。通常CLIと同じHOME・cwd・project/user/local設定・MCP・plugin・skill・permission/trustを共有する。aitermは完了相関stateだけをlaunch単位で所有する。起動されたagentにはsub-agent自己認識、親session、delegation depth/lineage、delegation_allowed=trueを注入し、必要な追加委譲は許可する。別のcomputer（登録済みの端末）で起こす時は、この起動にterminal（端末の登録元が渡す値をそのまま）とcwd（その端末のproject folder）を付ける。ここで起こしてからcd・sshしない。秘密の値はどの引数・prompt・送信文にも書かず、env_varsに名前だけを書く。通常settingsへlaunch固有Stop hook settingsを加算する。起動前に共有認証を構造化確認し、未認証ならsessionを作らない。dispatch した子は投げっぱなしでよい＝親はここで待たない。Codex親とClaude Code親にはAitermが回答本文を自動配送する。parent_deliveryがある場合はwait起動も通常の回答回収も不要。親は作業を続けるかターンを終える。Cursor親にはparent_deliveryとwait_processが付く。作業を続ければ次のツール返りに回答が差し込まれ、ターンを終える前にwait_processを背景で起動するとidle中の完了でも起きられる。ポーリングとpty_read(agent_transcript:true)は不要。その他の親では、完了通知をreceiptの `wait_process.executable` と `wait_process.args` をそのまま親のターンを塞がない別プロセスAPIへ渡して受け、PowerShell 7のStart-Processだけは `windows_start_process_argument_list` を単一文字列として渡す。exit を完了通知として扱う（exit 0=done / 3=timeout（既定600秒・未完了） / 4=closed / 7=error（harnessの記録でturnがAPIエラー等で打ち切られた。結果は無い）。receiptのoutcomeが正で、done以外は未完了。ポーリング不要）。`wait_command` は人間向け互換表示でありprocess境界へ使わない。foreground実行で親のターンを塞がない。自動配送以外の結果回収は pty_read(agent_transcript:true)。Claude の durable turn は claude_turn でも回収できる。

reasoning_effort.description: Claude Code reasoning effort。low/medium/high/xhigh/max。省略時はCLI既定

fast.description: ファスト（harnessの高速の応答。費用や利用量が増える）。省略とfalseは通常の速度で起こす（利用者の設定にfastが残っていても通常）。trueは通常で起こしてから、その席をfastへ切り替える。modelがfastに対応していない時（FAST_MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED）と、modelへfast版のIDを書いてfalseを渡した時（FAST_MODE_MODEL_CONFLICT）は起動を断る。アカウントの都合で使えない時・確かめられない時は、起動を断らずに通常の速度で起こし、返りの fast を false、fast_error に訳を入れる。modelへfast版のIDを直に書いて省略した時だけ、そのIDのまま起こす（返りの fast は true）。

terminal.description: Run this seat on another computer (a registered terminal) over SSH. Value: exactly the terminal value your host system's terminal registry hands over, {ref, target:{host,user,port}, os?, trustRevision, and credentialRevision or credential {handle, revision}}; copy it unchanged, never invent or edit it, never use a host name or ssh command instead. Omit it to launch on this computer. Give cwd in the same call: the absolute project folder on that terminal in its own form (a POSIX path starting with / on macOS and Linux, a drive path like C:\folder with backslashes on Windows). Never launch locally and then cd or ssh. Never put tokens, passwords or other secrets in any argument, prompt or typed text; pass secret values only by name in env_vars. After launch, use session_id alone for pty_send, pty_observe, pty_read, pty_key, claude_turn, agent_stop and pty_close; Aiterm routes them to the terminal. Errors and next step: TERMINAL_INVALID = malformed value, missing/relative cwd (or one in the other system's form), or combined with remote: pass the registry's value unchanged with cwd. TARGET_MISMATCH / BINDING_UNKNOWN = the value is not this terminal's binding: ask the terminal registry again. HOST_TRUST_STALE / CREDENTIAL_REVISION_STALE = the binding changed: get the current value from the terminal registry and launch again. HOST_KEY_MISMATCH / HOST_TRUST_MISSING = the terminal's host key is not the trusted one: the Owner must confirm the new host key; do not retry. CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED / CREDENTIAL_NOT_LOADED = this terminal's key comes from a credential handle that the registry must load first; never paste a key anywhere. AUTH_FAILED = the terminal refused the key. UNREACHABLE = the terminal is offline; try later. CONNECTION_REFUSED = the terminal refused the SSH connection (SSH may be off there); try later. REMOTE_AITERM_TOO_OLD = update Aiterm on the terminal. CWD_UNAVAILABLE = the folder does not exist there; do not pick another folder. SEAT_FORWARD_UNAVAILABLE = the seat's MCP route back to this computer is not ready (launch again later), or the seat MCP URLs are not http://127.0.0.1:<one port>/api/seat-mcp. All five harnesses run on a terminal; REMOTE_AITERM_TOO_OLD names the Aiterm version the harness needs there (claude-code 0.65.0, codex-cli 0.70.7, grok-cli / cursor-cli / antigravity-cli 0.70.9). TERMINAL_HARNESS_UNSUPPORTED = the harness name is none of the five. AGENT_LAUNCH_NOT_STARTED with _meta aiterm/launch_error code AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED = the CLI on the terminal is not logged in; the Owner logs it in there, then launch again. TERMINAL_OS_MISMATCH = the terminal is not the operating system os says: the registry's os is wrong or the binding points at another machine; ask the terminal registry, do not retry. TERMINAL_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED = the terminal is not a macOS, Linux or Windows system, so it cannot run seats.

Never launch locally and then cd or ssh. Never put tokens, passwords or other secrets in any argument, prompt or typed text; pass secret values only by name in env_vars. After launch, use session_id alone for pty_send, pty_observe, pty_read, pty_key, claude_turn, agent_stop and pty_close; Aiterm routes them to the terminal. Errors and next step: TERMINAL_INVALID = malformed value, missing/relative cwd (or one in the other system's form), or combined with remote: pass the registry's value unchanged with cwd. TARGET_MISMATCH / BINDING_UNKNOWN = the value is not this terminal's binding: ask the terminal registry again. HOST_TRUST_STALE / CREDENTIAL_REVISION_STALE = the binding changed: get the current value from the terminal registry and launch again. HOST_KEY_MISMATCH / HOST_TRUST_MISSING = the terminal's host key is not the trusted one: the Owner must confirm the new host key; do not retry. CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED / CREDENTIAL_NOT_LOADED = this terminal's key comes from a credential handle that the registry must load first; never paste a key anywhere. AUTH_FAILED = the terminal refused the key. UNREACHABLE = the terminal is offline; try later. CONNECTION_REFUSED = the terminal refused the SSH connection (SSH may be off there); try later. REMOTE_AITERM_TOO_OLD = update Aiterm on the terminal. CWD_UNAVAILABLE = the folder does not exist there; do not pick another folder. SEAT_FORWARD_UNAVAILABLE = the seat's MCP route back to this computer is not ready (launch again later), or the seat MCP URLs are not http://127.0.0.1:<one port>/api/seat-mcp. All five harnesses run on a terminal; REMOTE_AITERM_TOO_OLD names the Aiterm version the harness needs there (claude-code 0.65.0, codex-cli 0.70.7, grok-cli / cursor-cli / antigravity-cli 0.70.9). TERMINAL_HARNESS_UNSUPPORTED = the harness name is none of the five. AGENT_LAUNCH_NOT_STARTED with _meta aiterm/launch_error code AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED = the CLI on the terminal is not logged in; the Owner logs it in there, then launch again. TERMINAL_OS_MISMATCH = the terminal is not the operating system os says: the registry's os is wrong or the binding points at another machine; ask the terminal registry, do not retry. TERMINAL_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED = the terminal is not a macOS, Linux or Windows system, so it cannot run seats.

definition.name: pty_send
definition.description: セッションへテキストを送る。通常PTYへは送信のみ（出力は pty_read で取得）。agent session（launcher起動）への送信はこのtoolだけで行い、子の状態はAitermが送る時点で見て振り分ける。子のturnが実行中なら各harness標準の操作で現在のturnへ差し込み（mode=agent_steer）、完了は差し込み後の作業の終わりに元の依頼への1回だけ届く。新しいevent_cursorと配送は作らない。それ以外は新しいturnとしてdispatchし（mode=agent_dispatch）、TUI の ready gate と submit 分離を通して即返り、receipt の event_cursor を返す。dispatch した子は投げっぱなしでよい＝親はここで待たない。Codex親とClaude Code親にはAitermが回答本文を自動配送する。parent_deliveryがある場合はwait起動も通常の回答回収も不要。親は作業を続けるかターンを終える。Cursor親にはparent_deliveryとwait_processが付く。作業を続ければ次のツール返りに回答が差し込まれ、ターンを終える前にwait_processを背景で起動するとidle中の完了でも起きられる。ポーリングとpty_read(agent_transcript:true)は不要。その他の親では、完了通知をreceiptの `wait_process.executable` と `wait_process.args` をそのまま親のターンを塞がない別プロセスAPIへ渡して受け、PowerShell 7のStart-Processだけは `windows_start_process_argument_list` を単一文字列として渡す。exit を完了通知として扱う（exit 0=done / 3=timeout（既定600秒・未完了） / 4=closed / 7=error（harnessの記録でturnがAPIエラー等で打ち切られた。結果は無い）。receiptのoutcomeが正で、done以外は未完了。ポーリング不要）。`wait_command` は人間向け互換表示でありprocess境界へ使わない。foreground実行で親のターンを塞がない。自動配送以外の結果回収は pty_read(agent_transcript:true)、Claude の durable turn は claude_turn を使う。require_agent:true はagent登録が無いsessionへ打鍵せず、AGENT_SESSION_REQUIREDで未送信を返す。preface はagent sessionへの送信で本文の前に置く1行。Claude Codeの席では貼り付けの印なしで入れ、本文だけを貼る（前置きが貼り付けの包みの外へ出る）。他のharnessでは前置き・空行・本文を1つで貼る。force:true は非Claude agent sessionへの手動介入用の素送信。aiterm相関付きClaudeの承認UIはclaude_approvalを使う。

text.description: 送る文字列（コマンド／prompt）。UTF-8で最大64KiB

enter.description: 末尾で Enter を送る（agent dispatch では常に submit）

mark.description: 完了 sentinel(終了コード付き)で包む。pty_read(wait:true) が until 無しでも自動検出して完了確定する（POSIX shell と PowerShell に対応。SSH先の現在の標準PS promptも自動判定。PowerShell の rc は成功0／失敗1。fish/csh/tcsh は未対応として送信前に拒否）。 enter:false と併用すると sentinel が実行されず完了検出が発火しない（送信後に pty_key("Enter") で実行される）。

force.description: 非Claude agent sessionでは自動dispatchせず素送信する。aiterm相関付きClaudeのactive turnには使えない

require_agent.description: agent登録が無いsessionは打鍵前に拒否する。force:trueとは併用できない

preface.description: agent session への送信（forceなし）で、本文の前に置く1行。送る文は「preface・空行・text」の並びになる。Claude Codeの席ではprefaceを貼り付けの印なしで入れ、textだけを貼る。Codex／Grok／Cursor／Antigravityの席では1つで貼る。1行・200字以内・制御文字なしで、行頭が記号や空白でなく、@ を含まない文。外れた時と通常PTY送信・force送信・remote付きでは、打鍵前に拒否する

accessibility id: cross-platform, fast and stable. id: Android resource-id; iOS accessibility-id alias.

name: legacy; class name: broad matches; css selector: webview only.

Works on both iOS (simulators and real devices) and Android (emulators and real devices with mock location enabled). Use action=get to read current coordinates, action=set with latitude/longitude (and optional altitude for Android) to simulate a location, or action=reset to restore the system default. Note: On Android emulators, reset is not supported — use action=set to manually restore coordinates instead. On Android real devices, the mocked location may persist until the GPS cache refreshes.

action.description: Action to perform. get: read the current device geolocation. set: set the device geolocation (requires latitude and longitude; optional altitude for Android). reset: reset the geolocation to the default/system value. Not supported on Android emulators — use action=set instead.

latitude.description: Latitude value (-90 to 90). Measurement of distance north or south of the Equator. Required for: set.

longitude.description: Longitude value (-180 to 180). Measurement of distance east or west of the prime meridian. Required for: set.

definition.description: Perform a touch gesture. Use 'action' to choose: tap, double_tap, long_press, scroll, swipe, pinch_zoom, scroll_to_element, back. Choose scroll vs swipe by intent: scroll to browse content in a list or feed; swipe to dismiss, switch screens, navigate carousels, or pull-to-refresh (speed=fast). For drag-and-drop use appium_drag_and_drop. For custom multi-touch use appium_perform_actions.

action.description:
tap/double_tap/long_press: requires elementUUID or both x/y.
scroll/swipe: requires direction or x/y/endX/endY.
pinch_zoom: requires scale (<1 out, >1 in).
scroll_to_element: requires strategy/selector; direction up/down (default down).
Stops on a match, unchanged page source, or maxScrollAttempts. Adjust distance with scrollDistance or scrollDistancePreset.
back: system back navigation.

elementUUID.description: Element UUID for tap, double_tap, long_press, or pinch_zoom; overrides x/y for these actions. For scroll/swipe with direction, coordinates are calculated relative to this element instead of the whole screen.

x.description: X pixel coordinate, paired with y: tap location, pinch center, or scroll/swipe start (requires endX/endY). elementUUID overrides x/y for tap/double_tap/long_press/pinch_zoom.

y.description: Y pixel coordinate, paired with x; same action meanings and elementUUID precedence as x.

endX.description: Ending X coordinate in pixels for scroll/swipe; requires x, y, endY.

endY.description: Ending Y coordinate in pixels for scroll/swipe; requires x, y, endX.

direction.description: Direction for scroll/swipe. Coordinates are calculated from the screen or element bounds. Provide either direction or custom coordinates (x, y, endX, endY); direction takes precedence if both are given. For scroll_to_element, use up/down; default down.

speed.description: Swipe only. slow: deliberate drag; normal: default navigation speed; fast: flick without an initial hold. Use fast for pull-to-refresh and other velocity-sensitive interfaces.

duration.description: Duration in milliseconds. long_press defaults to 2000 (range 500–10000); scroll defaults to 800. For swipe, prefer speed unless a custom movement duration is needed. For W3C swipe, overrides movement time; speed still sets the initial hold. Ignored by iOS native mobile: swipe (direction, no elementUUID, speed != fast).

scale.description: Required for pinch_zoom: <1 zooms out, >1 zooms in (e.g. 0.5 or 2 for 2x).

velocity.description: Pinch velocity in scale factor per second. Default 2.2. Used by pinch_zoom.

definition.description: Manage Appium sessions. Use action=create to start a session, attach to connect to an existing one, detach to forget an attached session, delete to stop one, list to see all active sessions, or select to switch the active session.

action.description:
create: Create a new Appium session.
DEFAULT MODE (no remoteServerUrl): use unless the user explicitly provides a server URL.
- Drivers run embedded inside this MCP server; no separate Appium process is needed.
- Use select_device tool FIRST to discover devices. Ask for platform/device if unknown; do not assume a platform.
- For iOS simulators, run prepare_ios_simulator before creating the session.
- Call appium_session_management action=create with the selected platform and any returned capabilitiesHint serialized as capabilities.
- Do NOT pass remoteServerUrl for local/embedded mode. NEVER invent a localhost URL.
REMOTE SERVER MODE (only when user explicitly provides a URL):
- Skip local device selection and preparation; do not call select_device.
- Infer platform and device type from the request when possible; ask if unclear.
- Use platform=general for non-Android/iOS drivers (Windows, macOS, custom); capabilities pass through without platform defaults.
- Call appium_session_management action=create with platform, remoteServerUrl, and the requested capabilities.
- Example: "create an iOS session at http://localhost:4723" means platform=ios and remoteServerUrl=http://localhost:4723; do not discover local devices.
attach: connect to an existing remote Appium session without taking ownership of its lifecycle. Requires remoteServerUrl and sessionId; capabilities are fetched from the remote server.
detach: remove an attached session from MCP without deleting the real remote session. Defaults to the active session.
delete: delete a session and clean up resources. Defaults to the active session.
list: list managed sessions with active flag, ownership, and current context.
select: set sessionId as the active session for subsequent calls; requires sessionId.

platform.description: Required for create. For local sessions, match the platform selected via select_device. For remote sessions, infer from the request; general supports non-Android/iOS drivers (Windows, macOS, custom) and requires remoteServerUrl.

capabilities.description: Optional W3C capabilities as a JSON string, e.g. '{"appium:app":"/path/to/app","appium:platformVersion":"17.0"}'. Create: overrides defaults for ios/android; passed through as-is for general. Common keys: appium:app, appium:deviceName, appium:udid, appium:platformVersion, appium:bundleId. When using capabilitiesHint from a preparation tool, serialize the full object to JSON; preserve boolean and numeric values. Attach: optional fallback values (e.g. '{"platformName":"iOS"}'); capabilities fetched from the server take precedence.

remoteServerUrl.description: Remote Appium server URL for create or attach (e.g. http://localhost:4723). Omit to use local server for create.

sessionId.description: Required for attach and select: the existing session to connect to or activate. For delete: session to delete. For detach: attached session to forget without stopping it. Delete/detach default to the active session when omitted.

definition.name: bus_get_city_config
definition.title: Get city operating config
definition.description:
Get a city's runtime config: max poll interval and "arriving" time threshold.

This is mostly relevant if you are deciding how aggressively to refresh — not for end-user questions about lines or stops.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required): e.g. '034' (Shanghai), '027' (Beijing)
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "maxInterval": 30,
    "arrivingStationLimitSeconds": 180,
    "busDisplayConfig": { "lineDetail": "time#order#distance", "other": "time#order" }
  }

city_id.description: City ID, e.g. '034' for Shanghai, '027' for Beijing

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_line_detail
definition.title: Get full line detail (stops + live buses)
definition.description:
Full info for a line: rider-facing fields (name, first/last/price, stationsNum), the full ordered station list, the reverse-direction lineId, and every bus currently on the line.

**Use this — not bus_get_timetable — to answer "is line X still running" or "first/last bus time" questions.** The timetable tool only has data for a small minority of lines.

**Subway lines are NOT supported.** If bus_search returned a line with isSubway=true (e.g. lineId=1057 for 地铁2号线), this endpoint returns an empty payload — the response will carry `empty: true` and a `hint` field pointing at bus_get_nearby_stops / bus_plan_transit. Don't retry; route to those tools instead.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required): from bus_search.lines[*].lineId
  - lat / lng (string, optional): caller's WGS-84 coordinates
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "line": { "lineId":"...", "name":"71", "lineNo":"r95817", "direction":0, "startSn":"...", "endSn":"...", "firstTime":"05:30", "lastTime":"23:30", "price":"2元", "stationsNum":24 },
    "stations": [{ "order":1, "sId":"...", "sn":"...", "wgsLat":..., "wgsLng":..., "physicalStId":"...", "namesakeStId":"...", "metros":[{"name":"地铁14号线","lineNo":"14号线","color":"97,96,32"}] }, ...],
    "buses": [{ "busId":"...", "order":2, "lat":..., "lng":..., "speed":5.7, "capacity":0, "distanceToWaitStn":...}],
    "reverseDirection": { "lineId":"...", "startSn":"...", "endSn":"...", "firstTime":"04:30", "lastTime":"22:30", "price":"2元" } | null,
    "depDesc": "...", "preArrivalTime": "...", "targetOrder": 24,
    "empty": true, "hint": "..."   // present only when upstream returned no data (subway / retired line)
  }

Each station carries:
- 'order' → feed into bus_get_line_realtime / bus_list_line_buses as target_order
- 'sId' → feed into bus_get_line_realtime as station_id (NOT into bus_get_stop_detail!)
- 'physicalStId' + 'namesakeStId' → feed into bus_get_stop_detail to see every line through that stop

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_line_realtime
definition.title: Get realtime buses for a (line, stop) pair
definition.description:
Canonical "when will my bus arrive" tool. Returns every bus currently on the line, with the nearest one carrying an ETA to the waiting stop.

**Important**: the upstream predicts an ETA for only the nearest bus heading to your stop. Buses farther up the route are returned (with position/speed/capacity) but their `eta` field is null. That's not a bug.

**Args**:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required): from bus_search
  - target_order (string, required): the waiting stop's order on the line. Source: bus_get_line_detail.stations[i].order, or bus_get_nearby_stops.stops[].lines[].targetOrder.
  - station_id (string, required): sId of the waiting stop
  - lat / lng (string, required): WGS-84 — the user's location is best; if unavailable, use the waiting stop's wgsLat/wgsLng (from line_detail.stations[i]).
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "line": { "lineId":"...", "name":"71", "direction":0, "endSn":"..." },
    "targetOrder": 2,
    "realData": true,
    "buses": [
      { "busId":"...", "licence":"...", "order":2, "lat":..., "lng":..., "speed":5.7, "capacity":0, "distanceToWaitStn":90, "eta":{"travelTime":25,"arrivalTime":1779070466055,"displayTime":"10:14"} },
      { "busId":"...", "order":3, "lat":..., "lng":..., "speed":3, "capacity":0, "eta":null },
      ...
    ],
    "note": "..."
  }

Field notes:
- The 'line' sub-object intentionally omits startSn — upstream does not return it on this endpoint. Read it from bus_get_line_detail if needed.
- eta.travelTime is seconds remaining
- eta.arrivalTime is a ms timestamp
- eta.displayTime is a "HH:MM" hint from upstream
- capacity: 0=light, 1=moderate, 2=crowded

target_order.description: Order index of the waiting stop on the line. Get it from bus_get_line_detail.stations[].order or bus_get_nearby_stops.stops[].lines[].targetOrder.

lat.description: WGS-84 latitude. If the user's location is unknown, fall back to the waiting stop's lat (from line_detail.stations[].wgsLat).

lng.description: WGS-84 longitude. Fallback to the stop's wgsLng if unknown.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_line_route
definition.title: Get line polyline coordinates
definition.description:
Polyline coordinates for drawing a line on a map. Points with 'stopOrder' are actual stops; others are shape points between stops.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required)
  - include_shape (boolean, default false): false returns only stop markers (~25 points); true returns all shape points (~400-500). Skip unless you actually need to draw the line.
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "pointCount": 480,           // total shape points upstream returned
    "stopCount": 23,             // stop markers among them
    "points": [{ "lat":..., "lng":..., "stopOrder":1 }, ...]
  }
'points' is the filtered list — stops only by default, full polyline when include_shape=true.

**Known caveat**: upstream sometimes omits the terminus stop from the polyline, so 'stopCount' may be one less than bus_get_line_detail's 'stationsNum' (e.g. 23 vs 24). Trust bus_get_line_detail for the authoritative station list; line_route is just for drawing.

Markdown mode only summarises counts; request JSON to read coordinates.

include_shape.description: If true, include all polyline shape points (often 400-500 per line). Default false returns only stop-marker points.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_my_location
definition.title: Get the caller's approximate location via IP
definition.description:
Resolve the caller's approximate location from their public IP — useful when the user asks something like "what's near me" without providing coordinates.

**Precision is city-level (typically a few kilometres).** Good enough to identify the city and seed bus_get_nearby_stops with a starting guess. NOT precise enough to find the user's actual bus stop — for that, ask for a landmark/address and resolve it via bus_search.

Caveats:
  - Resolves via ip-api.com (free tier; rate-limited but no auth).
  - VPN / corporate proxy → result reflects the proxy exit IP, not the user.
  - Cellular IPs often land on a provincial centroid.

Args:
  - ip (string, optional): a specific IPv4/IPv6 to look up. Omit to use the mcp server process's own outbound IP (= the caller's machine when running locally).
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "lat": 31.2222,
    "lng": 121.4581,
    "gpsType": "wgs",
    "city": "上海",
    "region": "上海市",
    "country": "中国",
    "ip": "116.236.0.1",
    "isp": "China Telecom",
    "precision": "city-level (~10 km); not suitable for stop-level queries"
  }

**Suggested workflow**:
  1. Call this tool to identify the user's city (match 'city' field against bus_list_cities to get a cityId).
  2. Pass lat/lng into bus_get_nearby_stops for a rough nearby list, OR ask the user to confirm a landmark and use bus_search.pois for sharper coordinates.

ip.description: Optional override IP to look up. Omit to use the mcp server's own outbound IP (i.e. the caller's machine).

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_nearby_stops
definition.title: Get nearby bus stops

limit.description: How many of the nearest stops to return. Default 5 — the upstream may return 15+ and most callers only care about the closest few.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_stop_detail
definition.title: Get stop detail with all lines
definition.description:
Full detail for a stop: precise WGS-84 coordinates, every line that passes through (with first/last/price), realtime buses, and nearby metro lines.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - physical_st_id (string, required): from bus_get_nearby_stops / bus_search
  - namesake_st_id (string, optional): recommended; from the same source
  - first_line_id (string, optional): a line to highlight
  - lat / lng (string, optional): caller's WGS-84 location, used to populate 'distance'
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "stations": [
      { "sId": "...", "sn": "...", "lat": ..., "lng": ..., "distance": ...,
        "lines": [{ "lineId": "...", "name": "71", "direction": 0, "startSn": "...", "endSn": "...", "firstTime": "05:30", "lastTime": "23:30", "price": "2元", "targetOrder": 2, "buses": [...] }],
        "metros": [{ "name": "地铁14号线", "lineNo": "14号线", "color": "97,96,32" }] }
    ]
  }

Multiple entries in stations[] mean the stop name maps to several physical platforms.

physical_st_id.description: physicalStId of the stop (from bus_get_nearby_stops or bus_search)

first_line_id.description: Optional hint of a line you want highlighted

lat.description: Caller's WGS-84 latitude — used to populate 'distance'

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_timetable
definition.title: Get a line's per-trip schedule (rarely useful)
definition.description:
Per-trip departure schedule for a line. The upstream returns one of three modes via `mode`:
  - 'scheduled' (timeTableType=1): an explicit `timetable` array of trips
  - 'interval' (timeTableType=2): the line runs at a fixed headway — NO per-trip times are returned
  - 'special' / 'unknown' (timeTableType=3 or other)

**Most lines in Shanghai are 'interval'**, so this tool is rarely the right one. To answer "first/last bus", "is the line still running", or "what's the next departure", call **bus_get_line_detail** instead — it always returns firstTime / lastTime / price / live buses.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required)
  - line_no (string, required): rider-facing short name from bus_search.lines[].name (e.g. '71'). Do NOT pass the internal lineNo like 'r95817'.
  - direction ('0'|'1'): the line direction
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "line": { "lineId":"...", "name":"71", "direction":0, "startSn":"...", "endSn":"..." },
    "timeTableType": 2,
    "mode": "interval",
    "timetable": null,
    "note": "This line runs at a fixed interval — ..."
  }

line_no.description: Rider-facing short name (search.lines[].name), e.g. '71'. NOT the internal lineNo like 'r95817'.

definition.name: bus_plan_transit
definition.title: Plan a public-transit route
definition.description:
Plan a public-transit (bus + metro) route between two points. Returns alternative plans sorted by recommendation, each broken into walking and ride segments.

**Coordinate system**: this tool expects GCJ-02. The easiest source is bus_search.pois[*].lat/lng — those are already GCJ-02 and carry a name. If you only have WGS-84 (e.g. from a phone GPS), convert it before calling.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - origin_name, origin_lat, origin_lng (string, required): origin in GCJ-02
  - dest_name, dest_lat, dest_lng (string, required): destination in GCJ-02
  - strategy ('0'|'1'|'2'|'3'): 0=recommended (default; surfaces metro), 1=fewest transfers, 2=least walking, 3=shortest time (BUS-ONLY — upstream often drops metro plans here, so for general "fastest route" questions use 0)
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "origin": "lng,lat",
    "destination": "lng,lat",
    "distance": 17982,
    "plans": [
      {
        "duration": 3056, "walkingDistance": 1466, "distance": 19086, "tag": "直达", "transitCount": 1,
        "segments": [
          { "type": "walking", "distance": 837, "duration": 717 },
          { "type": "bus", "name": "地铁2号线", "lineType": 1, "departureStop": "人民广场", "arrivalStop": "虹桥2号航站楼", "viaStops": 8, "duration": 1800, "distance": 17620, "startTime": "05:37", "endTime": "23:30" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }

A top-level 'note' field is emitted when the response shape is suspicious — e.g. strategy=3 returned no metro plans despite this being a likely metro trip.

definition.name: bus_search
definition.title: Search lines, stations, and POIs
definition.description:
Search inside a city by keyword. Returns matching lines, stations, and POIs in one call.

Use this as the primary entry point when the user gives a line number, station name, or destination name without IDs.

**Keyword tip**: plain "71", "71路", "地铁2号线", "陆家嘴" all work — the upstream is reasonably forgiving. If a short numeric returns empty, try appending "路".

**Coordinate systems**:
  - 'pois' coords are GCJ-02 (use directly with bus_plan_transit)
  - 'stations' coords are WGS-84 (use with bus_get_nearby_stops / bus_get_line_realtime)
  Both are also marked with a 'gpsType' field.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required): e.g. '034'
  - keyword (string, required)
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "highlightKey": "71路",
    "lines": [
      {
        "name": "71", "lineNo": "r95817", "isSubway": false,
        "directions": [
          { "direction": 0, "lineId": "21283603183", "startSn": "延安东路外滩", "endSn": "申昆路枢纽站" },
          { "direction": 1, "lineId": "21283603182", "startSn": "申昆路枢纽站", "endSn": "延安东路外滩" }
        ],
        // Compat top-level fields mirror directions[0] (or first available).
        "lineId": "21283603183", "direction": 0, "startSn": "延安东路外滩", "endSn": "申昆路枢纽站"
      },
      ...
    ],
    "stations": [{ "sId":"...", "sn":"西藏中路", "lat":31.231006, "lng":121.474316, "gpsType":"wgs", "physicalStId":"...", "namesakeStId":"...", "isSubway":false }, ...],
    "pois": [{ "name":"71路", "address":"...", "tag":"公交线路", "district":"黄浦区", "lat":31.233021, "lng":121.49073, "gpsType":"gcj" }, ...]
  }

**Line folding**: each entry in 'lines' is one logical line (e.g. "71路"). The two travel directions live in 'directions[]'. Pick the lineId matching your desired direction.

**Subway hint**: when 'isSubway' is true, the entry carries a 'hint' field — bus_get_line_detail will return empty for these lineIds. Use bus_get_stop_detail (metros field) or bus_plan_transit instead.

**Follow-ups**:
- directions[i].lineId → bus_get_line_detail (full stop list, first/last/price) — non-subway only
- stations[*].physicalStId + namesakeStId → bus_get_stop_detail
  (NOTE: a few stations lack physicalStId — typically metro-only entries with subwayV2=1. For those, use bus_get_nearby_stops to resolve the bus platform IDs nearby.)
- pois[*].lat/lng (GCJ) → bus_plan_transit as origin/destination

keyword.description: Search keyword. Examples: '71', '71路', '地铁2号线', '陆家嘴', '人民广场'. Plain line numbers like '71' work fine.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.description: Set the complete set of logpoints of the selected page: logpoints not in the list are removed, new ones are added, and an empty list removes all. A logpoint logs expressions to the console every time a line executes, without pausing or changing the source, like logpoints in the DevTools Sources panel. Locations are script URLs or original source files resolved through source maps (not available with --no-source-maps; scripts in workers and out-of-process iframes are not supported). A location in a generated script moves to its original source line when a source map covers it, and locations on the same line become one logpoint with the last expression. Output appears in list_console_messages; an expression that throws produces an error message without text. Logpoints survive reloads and navigations until removed or the page is closed. The response lists the resulting logpoints and where they are bound.

The url is a script URL or the path of an original source file from a source map, exact or as a path suffix (e.g. "src/app.ts"). Line and column numbers are 1-based in the coordinates of the url; a line without executable code moves to the next possible location. The expression is evaluated like console.log() arguments in the scope of the location, where local variables are accessible by their original names, and runs before the line executes, so a variable declared on that line is not set yet. list_console_messages shows objects as [object Object]: read them with get_console_message, or log JSON.stringify(value) for plain data. Example: "src/cart.ts:42 'cart total:', cart.total, cart.items.length". Pass an empty array to remove all logpoints.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of the file input element or an element that will open file chooser on the page from the page content snapshot

filePaths.description: One or more files paths to upload. File paths have to be local to the browser instance (not the MCP).

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

definition.name: wait_for
definition.description: Wait for the specified text to appear on the selected page. By default, hidden text is also matched. Set visible to true to wait until the matched text is visible.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

text.description: Non-empty list of texts. Resolves when any value matches an accessible name exactly or is a substring of DOM text. Matching is case-sensitive. DOM text preserves spaces and newlines, unlike snapshot text which may normalize whitespace. Use the original whitespace or a shorter distinctive substring.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

visible.description: If true, wait until the matching text is visible. By default, hidden text also counts.

server_info.name: color-space
server_info.description: Conversions between 221 color spaces, each tested against a cited reference

definition.name: code
definition.title: Library code
definition.description: The conversion as code to paste: the color-space JS call with its result and – where one exists for the space on the non-sRGB side – the colour-science (Python) equivalent verified against color-space (sRGB ↔ that space), with any named caveat. The color goes in as a CSS string or as values in `from` (default: sRGB 200, 100, 50).

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

to.description: target space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

values.description: the color in the source space

definition.name: convert
definition.title: Convert color
definition.description: Convert a color between any two of the 221 color spaces, identity included, in each space's conventional ranges (rgb 0-255, oklch L 0-1 / C 0-0.4 / H 0-360, lab L 0-100 …). The color goes in as a CSS string (`color`) or as channel values (`from` + `values`); a batch as `colors` – tuples in `from`, CSS strings, or both. Out-of-range in, unclamped out: `inRange` flags each channel against the target's conventional range (rgb below 0 means outside sRGB); null = undefined at that coordinate.

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

to.description: target space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

values.description: one color in the source space, e.g. [255, 128, 0] for rgb

colors.description: a batch: one tuple (in `from`) or CSS string per color, e.g. [[255, 128, 0], '#00ff80', 'oklch(0.7 0.1 50)']

definition.name: css
definition.title: CSS color strings
definition.description: A color as CSS Color 4 strings — rgb(), hsl(), hwb(), lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch() and color(display-p3 | a98-rgb | prophoto-rgb | rec2020 | srgb-linear | xyz-d65 | xyz-d50) — plus #hex inside sRGB. Converted, never gamut-mapped: a string is null where CSS would clamp it into a different color (rgb/hsl/hwb outside sRGB, lightness out of range). `gamut` is the smallest display gamut that holds the color.

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

values.description: one color in the source space

notations.description: only these, by library space id (default: all)

definition.name: cube
definition.title: .cube LUT
definition.description: Render a conversion as a .cube LUT file (Resolve, Premiere, Final Cut, OBS, ffmpeg). The header carries the measured deviation vs the direct conversion. Pure per-channel transfers auto-emit 1D. Size ≤ 33 here (larger via the library or https://color-space.io/).

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

to.description: target space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

size.description: 3D lattice size (default 17)

definition.name: gamut
definition.title: Gamut membership
definition.description: Which standard display gamuts hold a color — sRGB ⊂ Display P3 ⊂ Rec. 2020, each tested in its own RGB box straight from the source space, the same ladder as the color-space.io gamut pill. `smallest` is the tightest one; null = beyond Rec. 2020. Membership only: nothing is gamut-mapped.

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

values.description: one color in the source space

definition.name: icc
definition.title: ICC profile
definition.description: One space as an ICC v2 profile (.icc): matrix + tone curve where the space is an RGB working space (Photoshop, OS color management), a CLUT on a Lab PCS otherwise (lcms, ArgyllCMS, ImageMagick). Returned as a base64 embedded resource; `class`, `pcs` and `bytes` describe it.

name.description: the space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

grid.description: CLUT lattice points per channel, CLUT profiles only (default 33 for 3 channels; fewer = a smaller file)

definition.name: shader
definition.title: Shader code
definition.description: The conversion as shader source – GLSL (WebGL2; WebGL1 too unless the path reads a table), WGSL (WebGPU), HLSL (DirectX, Unity, Unreal) or MSL (Metal) – with an entry function `<from>_<to>` (hyphens stripped), e.g. `vec3 rgb_oklch(vec3 c)`, plus every function on the path. Each language is differentially tested against the library and compiled on real GPUs: use it instead of writing color matrices. HLSL and MSL need the optional peer `naga-wasm` installed beside color-space.

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

to.description: target space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

definition.name: space
definition.title: Space dossier
definition.description: The dossier of one color space: display name (as color-space.io shows it), description, channels + conventional ranges, defining references, provenance (year, author), illuminant/observer, encoding class, family and purpose, and its direct conversion neighbours.

name.description: the space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 221)

definition.name: spaces
definition.title: Space catalog
definition.description: List the 221 color spaces with display name, family, purpose, channels and one-line use. Optional filters: `query` (words matched against id, name, use line and description; best matches first), `family`, `purpose`.

query.description: free text, e.g. 'camera log', 'cielab', 'display p3'

resources.name: data.json
resources.title: The 221-space catalog
resources.description: Every space: channels and ranges, references, provenance, gamuts, cited conformance points – the language-neutral artifact.

resource_templates.name: space
resource_templates.title: Space dossier
resource_templates.description: One space's dossier (the `space` tool's output), e.g. color-space://space/oklch

definition.name: cancel_job
definition.description: Cancel a queued extraction job. Has no effect on jobs that are already running.

definition.name: check_contrast
definition.description: Grade colour pairs against WCAG 2.1 contrast, at the threshold the text size earns: 18pt, or 14pt bold, is large scale and needs 3:1 where body text needs 4.5:1. Takes pairs you name, so it grades colours you are about to ship rather than only colours already on a page. Returns the ratio, the required ratio, and the AA and AAA verdicts per pair. Pure and synchronous, no browser. For pairs already rendered on a site, extract with wcag instead.

background.description: Background it sits on, hex or rgb()

fontSizePx.description: Rendered size in px. Without it the pair is graded as body text

label.description: Your own name for the pair, echoed back

definition.name: check_robots
definition.description: Ask whether robots.txt allows extracting a URL, before spending a browser run on it. Returns the verdict, the rule that decided it, and the robots.txt status. A 404 or 410 means no robots.txt and everything is allowed; any other unreadable response is treated as a refusal. Cheap and synchronous: one HTTP request, no browser.

url.description: The URL you intend to extract

definition.name: compute_drift
definition.description: Compare two dembrandt extractions and return a design-drift report: a 0-100 score (0 = identical), a stable/drift verdict, per-category scores, and the list of changed/added/removed tokens (colors, typography, spacing, radius, shadows). Pure and synchronous, no browser. Takes either an inline extraction or the job_id of a completed one. Use it to check whether generated or updated UI has drifted from a brand baseline.

baseline.description: A dembrandt extraction object. Omit it and pass job_id instead to read a completed extraction straight out of the job queue, which avoids sending the whole extraction back through the model.

candidate.description: A dembrandt extraction object. Omit it and pass job_id instead to read a completed extraction straight out of the job queue, which avoids sending the whole extraction back through the model.

baselineJobId.description: job_id of a completed extraction to read instead of passing result inline

candidateJobId.description: job_id of a completed extraction to read instead of passing result inline

failThreshold.description: Score above this yields a 'drift' verdict (default 10)

definition.name: export_dtcg
definition.description: Convert a dembrandt extraction to W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) format: color, typography, spacing, radius, border, and shadow tokens with $type/$value structure and dembrandt provenance under $extensions. Pure and synchronous, no browser. Takes either an inline extraction or the job_id of a completed one. Use it to hand tokens to Style Dictionary, Figma token plugins, or any DTCG-compatible pipeline.

result.description: A dembrandt extraction object. Omit it and pass job_id instead to read a completed extraction straight out of the job queue, which avoids sending the whole extraction back through the model.

job_id.description: job_id of a completed extraction to read instead of passing result inline

definition.description: Render a shadcn/ui theme from a dembrandt extraction: the :root block and the @theme inline mapping Tailwind v4 needs. A slot is written only where the page supplied a value, and the rest are named in the file header and left at shadcn's own defaults, so no slot is filled with an invented value that reads as measured. Pure and synchronous, no browser. Takes either an inline extraction or the job_id of a completed one.

definition.name: get_brand_identity
definition.description: Extract brand identity from a live website: site name, logo (source, dimensions, safe zone), all favicon variants (icon, apple-touch-icon, og:image, twitter:image with sizes and URLs), what builds the UI with versions where recoverable (JS and meta frameworks, CSS frameworks, component libraries, site builders), icon systems, and responsive breakpoints. Returns a job_id by default: poll it with get_job_status, and pass the same job_id to compute_drift, get_findings, export_dtcg, generate_design_md or render_report instead of resending the extraction.

definition.name: get_findings
definition.description: Lint a dembrandt extraction for design-system quality issues: WCAG contrast failures, inconsistency (near-duplicate colors, off-scale spacing values, radius sprawl), and duplication. Returns findings with severity (error/warn), category, and a human-readable message, plus summary counts. Pure and synchronous, no browser. Takes either an inline extraction or the job_id of a completed one. Complements compute_drift: drift asks 'did it change', findings asks 'is it good'.

definition.name: validate_dtcg
definition.description: Validate a W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) document against the 2025.10 spec: token types, colour objects and their component ranges, dimensions, references, and property-level $ref pointers. definition.name: execute_partiql
definition.description: Execute a PartiQL statement. Supports SELECT (with LIMIT, nested paths), INSERT (with IF NOT EXISTS, parameter placeholders), UPDATE (with SET arithmetic, REMOVE, nested paths), DELETE. UPDATE and DELETE accept a RETURNING clause, surfaced in the response Items: DELETE allows only RETURNING ALL OLD * (returning the deleted item; other variants are rejected), UPDATE allows all four RETURNING <ALL|MODIFIED> <OLD|NEW> * variants. WHERE supports BETWEEN, IN, CONTAINS, IS MISSING, IS NOT MISSING, AND, OR, NOT, parenthesised grouping up to 64 levels deep, and nested paths; AND binds tighter than OR, and a NOT over a group is applied by De Morgan. An index is named in the FROM clause as "table"."index", which serves the read from that GSI or LSI on SELECT only; a write statement rejects the qualifier. An UPDATE or DELETE whose WHERE condition fails is a ConditionalCheckFailedException; with return_values_on_condition_check_failure set to ALL_OLD the error carries the item the condition was evaluated against. Write statements are blocked in read-only mode.

consistent_read.description: Whether to use strongly consistent reads. Does not change which rows come back, but it doubles the rate a SELECT is charged at and it makes a SELECT qualified by a GSI a rejection, because a GSI cannot serve one.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to evaluate for SELECT statements (not necessarily the number returned); a filtered page can come back short or empty and still carry a NextToken

next_token.description: Continuation token from a previous SELECT response, to fetch the next page. Pass back the NextToken the last call returned; its absence means there are no more pages. The statement must stay identical character for character across pages, and so must the parameters; a token replayed with any difference is rejected with a ValidationException. A statement with a list or map parameter cannot be paged past its first page, as on DynamoDB.

parameters.description: Positional parameters for the statement, in DynamoDB JSON format

return_consumed_capacity.description: What consumed capacity to return: TOTAL for the operation's total, INDEXES for the total broken down by table and index, or NONE (the default) for none. Figures follow DynamoDB's charging rules and match what the DynamoDB API returns for the same request.

return_values_on_condition_check_failure.description: What to return when an UPDATE or DELETE fails its WHERE condition: ALL_OLD hands back the item the condition was evaluated against as the error's item; NONE, the default, does not. Any other value is rejected with a ValidationException.

statement.description: PartiQL statement to execute. Supports SELECT (with LIMIT, nested path projections, and NextToken paging), INSERT (with IF NOT EXISTS, parameter placeholders), UPDATE (with SET arithmetic, REMOVE, nested paths), DELETE. WHERE supports BETWEEN, IN, CONTAINS, IS MISSING, IS NOT MISSING, AND, OR, NOT, parenthesised grouping up to 64 levels deep, and nested paths; AND binds tighter than OR, and a NOT over a group is applied by De Morgan. An index is named in the FROM clause as "table"."index", which serves the read from that GSI or LSI on SELECT only; a write statement rejects the qualifier.

A RETURNING clause is not supported inside a transaction and is rejected with a ValidationException. Example transact_statements: [{"Statement": "INSERT INTO Users VALUE {'pk': 'u1', 'name': 'Alice'}"}]

definition.name: search_vectors
definition.description: [READ] Search a vector index for the nearest entries to a query vector. Exact brute-force KNN over the whole index, so the top-k is the true top-k. COSINE and EUCLIDEAN score as distances, where a self match is 0; DOT_PRODUCT scores as a similarity and can be negative. The vector attribute is excluded from results unless a projection_expression names it and the index projects it. Create the index with create_table's vector_indexes, which is searchable at once. An index added later through update_table refuses with 'Cannot search backfilling vector index' until it settles, for longer than describe_table reports it CREATING, so retry the search rather than waiting for the status.

Where the project has no e2e config file, pass engine to open a session on that engine: {engine: "@e2e-dev/web", app: {url: "http://localhost:3000"}}. With test, it runs that one test first and stops on the screen where the test passed or failed, with the failure and its line ahead of the catalog. Several sessions can be open at once, one per agent, each with its own engine: pass the returned session id to every later call. Then act with call and look with call {tool: "observe"}.

The session then stays on the screen where the test stopped; afterEach hooks and fixture teardown run at close_session. To rerun after editing the test, close_session and open_session with test again

An object passes options, and an option can be another factory call, which is how an engine gets a device or browser provider: {package: "@e2e-dev/mobile", options: {platform: "ios"}}, or {package: "@e2e-dev/mobile", options: {platform: "ios", device: {package: "@e2e-dev/limrun", export: "limrun", options: {region: "eu"}}}} for mobile({platform: "ios", device: limrun({region: "eu"})}). A package not installed fails with the command that installs it. Excludes target, config, and test

definition.name: run_tests
definition.description: Run tests as npx e2e run does and return what it printed: each test, the failures with their code frames, and the summary. Without files it runs every test the config discovers; files narrows to a test file, a directory, a glob, or one test (tests/checkout.e2e.ts:12). definition.name: analyze
definition.description: Analyze a TypeScript/JavaScript project for unused code and dependency cycles. On a Rust root, it runs `cargo fallow check` (deps, visibility; no score) and takes only root. Detects unused files, exports, types, dependencies, enum/class members, unresolved imports, unlisted dependencies, duplicate exports, circular dependencies, re-export cycles (barrel files that form a structural loop, silently breaking re-exports), package cycles (workspace packages that import each other in a loop), boundary violations, rule-pack policy violations (banned calls, imports, and catalogue-derived effects declared via the rulePacks config key), stale suppression comments, missing suppression reasons when rules.require-suppression-reason is enabled, unused pnpm catalog entries (entries in pnpm-workspace.yaml `catalog:` / `catalogs:` not referenced by any workspace package), empty pnpm catalog groups, unresolved catalog references (workspace package.json declares `catalog:` but the catalog has no entry), unused dependency overrides (entries in `pnpm-workspace.yaml#overrides`, `package.json#pnpm.overrides`, top-level `package.json#overrides`, or Bun `package.json#resolutions` whose target package no workspace package declares and the active readable lockfile does not resolve), and misconfigured dependency overrides (unparsable key or empty value; the active package manager may reject or ignore the entry). Opt-in issue_types: ["private-type-leaks"] (API hygiene), ["deprecated-exports-in-use"] (@deprecated in use), ["absent-component-props"] (optional-prop review), ["constant-parameters"] (parameter review). Returns structured JSON with all issues found, grouped by issue type. Each finding has a stable `finding_id`; an id absent from a scoped or differently configured run means unknown, not resolved. For code duplication use find_dupes, for complexity hotspots use check_health. Supports baselines, regression detection, performance tuning, boundary_violations, and group_by. Read the `fallow://tools/analyze` resource for the boundary_violations alias, the group_by modes, and how to dispatch the `next_steps[]` follow-up commands.

definition.name: audit
definition.description: Audit changed files for dead code, complexity, duplication, styling, and diff risk. Purpose-built for reviewing AI-generated code. Combines the analyses scoped to changed files and returns a verdict (pass/warn/fail). Auto-detects the base branch if not specified. By default, audit runs the base ref too and gates only findings introduced by the changeset; inherited findings are annotated with introduced=false and counted under attribution. Set gate="all" or audit.gate="all" in config to gate every finding. Returns JSON with verdict, summary counts per category, attribution counts, and full issue details with actions array for remediation guidance. Per-analysis payloads nest under `dead_code`, `duplication`, and `complexity`; the `complexity` block carries the health sub-analysis output (audit JSON has no `health` key). The `diff_risk` section reports facts about the change itself, such as weakened tests, added suppressions, and a clone copy edited without its siblings. Styling analytics are on by default. Read the fallow://tools/audit guide for the diff-risk rules, styling, coverage, synthetic complexity units, grouping, baselines, runtime coverage, and `FALLOW_DIFF_FILE` scoping. Use this after generating code to verify quality before committing.

definition.name: check_health
definition.description: Check code health metrics (cyclomatic and cognitive complexity) for functions in the project. Returns structured JSON with complexity scores per function, sorted by severity. On a Rust root, it runs `cargo fallow complexity` (max_cyclomatic, max_cognitive; no score). Set score=true for a single 0-100 health score with letter grade (A/B/C/D/F); runs duplication analysis automatically, but the churn-backed hotspot penalty requires hotspots=true (or targets=true). Set min_score=N to fail only when the score drops below a threshold (CI quality gate); min_score is authoritative, so complexity findings become informational and min_score=0 never fails. Exit codes are not surfaced over MCP, but the verdict is: a gated run publishes `gate_outcomes`, where `health-min-score` and `health-min-severity` carry a status, whether it was enforced, and the numbers compared. min_severity composes with min_score. Set file_scores=true for per-file health scores (maintainability index, fan-in, fan-out, dead code ratio, complexity density, CRAP risk), sorted in risk-aware triage order so lower MI and higher CRAP risk appear first. Set css=true to add a `css_analytics` section (specificity hotspots, `!important` density, over-complex selectors, deep nesting, design-token sprawl, unreferenced custom properties and `@keyframes`); opt-in because it parses every project stylesheet. Set complexity_breakdown=true to add a per-decision-point `contributions[]` array to each complexity finding, so you can explain WHY a function scored high and which lines to refactor. Set coverage_gaps=true to explicitly include static test coverage gaps: runtime files and exports with no test dependency path (not line-level coverage). A provided config file may also enable coverage gaps via rules.coverage-gaps when no health sections are explicitly selected. Set hotspots=true to identify files that are both complex and frequently changing (combines git churn with complexity). Set churn_file to a `fallow-churn/v1` JSON path to power the churn-backed signals (hotspots, ownership, refactoring targets) from imported VCS history instead of git. Set ownership=true (implies hotspots) to attach per-file ownership signals: bus factor, contributor count, declared CODEOWNERS owner, ownership_state, drift, and unowned-hotspot flag. Use ownership_email_mode=raw|handle|anonymized|hash for author email privacy (default handle; hash is the legacy spelling for anonymized output). Set targets=true for ranked refactoring recommendations sorted by efficiency (quick wins first), with confidence scores and adaptive percentile-based thresholds. Set trend=true to compare current metrics against the most recent saved snapshot and show per-metric deltas with directional indicators (improving/declining/stable). Implies --score. Requires prior snapshots saved with save_snapshot. Set effort to control analysis depth: 'low' (fast, surface-level), 'medium' (balanced, default), or 'high' (thorough, all heuristics). Set summary=true to include a natural-language summary of findings alongside the structured JSON. Set coverage to a path to Istanbul-format coverage data (coverage-final.json from Jest, Vitest, c8, nyc) for accurate per-function CRAP scores instead of the default estimated coverage. CRAP findings carry a `coverage_source` discriminator and the summary reports whether emitted sources are uniform or mixed. Besides real functions, health scores synthetic `<template>`, `<snippet:NAME>`, `<module>`, and Angular `<component>` rollup units, each with its own suppression placement and dimension rules. Set runtime_coverage to a path (V8 coverage directory, V8 JSON file, or Istanbul JSON file) for merged runtime-coverage findings (a single local capture is free; continuous or multi-capture runtime monitoring requires an active license via `fallow license activate`). Runtime-coverage tuning: set min_invocations_hot=N to tune the hot-path threshold (default 100), min_observation_volume=N to tune the high-confidence verdict floor (default 5000), and low_traffic_threshold=RATIO to tune the active/low-traffic split (default 0.001). Set group_by to "owner" (CODEOWNERS), "directory", "package" (workspace), or "section" (GitLab CODEOWNERS `[Section]` headers, with `owners` metadata per group) to partition results. Each group recomputes its own metrics against its files. When config health.thresholdOverrides is set, health findings use the resolved local thresholds and JSON includes threshold_overrides state so agents can see active, stale, and full-run no-match exceptions. For code duplication use find_dupes, for changed-file review use audit, and for execution-backed dead-or-hot verdicts use check_runtime_coverage. Read the `fallow://tools/check_health` resource for the per-flag detail this summary omits: the per-group metrics, `css_analytics` contents, `contributions[]` entries, the React `react_hook_profile` and render-fan-in vital signs, churn-file import, `coverage_source` values, the synthetic `<template>` / `<snippet:NAME>` / `<module>` / `<component>` units and their suppression placements, and the `threshold_overrides` row semantics. Supports config, baseline comparisons, and performance tuning (no_cache, threads). Useful for identifying hard-to-maintain code and prioritizing refactoring.
